sentences.zh: 欒共子曰：「民生於三，事之如一，唯其所在，則致死焉。」

translations.literal: Duke Gongzi of Luan said: "A person's life rests on three [bonds]; one serves them as one. Wherever one's [duty] lies, one dies for it."
translations.idiomatic: Duke Gongzi of Luan said, "A person's life rests on three fundamental bonds, and one should serve each with equal devotion. Wherever one's duty lies, one should be ready to die for it there."

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫居其位，食其祿，國家有難，在朝者死其官，守郡邑者死城郭，治軍旅者死行陣，市井草野之臣發憤而死，皆其所也。

translations.literal: When grandees and officials occupy their posts and eat their stipends, and the state faces peril, those at court die in their offices, those guarding commanderies and districts die at the walls and ramparts, those directing armies die in battle formations, and commoners of market and field die in righteous wrath—all in their proper places."
translations.idiomatic: When ministers and officials hold their posts and draw their salaries, and the realm is in crisis, those at court die at their posts, magistrates die defending walls and cities, commanders die in the ranks, and humble folk of town and countryside die in indignant sacrifice—each in the station that is theirs."

sentences.zh: 故死得其所，則所欲有甚於生者焉。

translations.literal: Therefore, when one dies in one's proper place, what one desires may exceed what one desires for life itself.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when one dies where one ought, what one seeks in death can outweigh what one seeks in life.

sentences.zh: 金代褒死節之臣，既贈官爵，仍錄用其子孫。

translations.literal: The Jin dynasty, in commending ministers who died loyal, not only bestowed posthumous offices and ranks but also recruited their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin, those who died loyal were not only posthumously ennobled but their descendants were also brought into service.

sentences.zh: 貞祐以來，其禮有加，立祠樹碑，歲時致祭，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenyou era, the rites for them have been increased: temples have been built, steles erected, and sacrifices offered at the seasons—indeed, it may be said to be utmost.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenyou period on, the honors grew—shrines and steles, seasonal sacrifices—reaching the highest degree of reverence.

sentences.zh: 聖元詔修遼、金、宋史，史臣議凡例，凡前代之忠於所事者，請書之無諱，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The sacred Yuan issued an edict to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song. The historians drafting the general rules proposed that loyal men of former dynasties to their lords should be written without reservation, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan ordered the compilation of the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, the compilers proposed that men loyal to their lords in earlier dynasties be recorded without omission, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 烏乎，仁哉聖元之為政也。

translations.literal: Alas, how benevolent was the sacred Yuan's governance!
translations.idiomatic: Ah, how humane was the governance of the sacred Yuan!

sentences.zh: 司馬遷記豫讓對趙襄子之言曰：「人主不掩人之美，而忠臣有成名之義。」

translations.literal: Sima Qian recorded Yu Rang's words to Zhao Xiangzi: "A ruler does not conceal men's merits, and loyal ministers have the principle of achieving a name."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian records Yu Rang telling Zhao Xiangzi, "A lord does not conceal others' worth, and a loyal minister has the right to win a lasting name."

sentences.zh: 至哉斯言，聖元之為政，足為萬世訓矣。

translations.literal: How supreme are these words! The governance of the sacred Yuan suffices as instruction for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: How profound that saying is! The Yuan's policy in this regard is a lesson for all ages."

sentences.zh: 作《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: [The author] composed "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 胡沙補

translations.literal: Hu Shabu
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shabu

sentences.zh: 胡沙補，完顏部人。

translations.literal: Hu Shabu was a man of the Wanyan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shabu was of the Wanyan clan.

sentences.zh: 年三十五從軍，頗見任用。

translations.literal: At age thirty-five he entered the army and was much employed.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-five he took the field and won substantial trust.

sentences.zh: 太祖使僕刮剌往遼國請阿竦，實觀其形勢。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Puguala to the Liao state to request Asong, in reality to observe their situation.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Puguala to the Liao court to request Asong, but in truth to scout their strength.

sentences.zh: 僕刮剌還言遼兵不知其數，太祖疑之，使胡沙補往。

translations.literal: Puguala returned saying he did not know the number of Liao troops; the Founder doubted this and sent Hu Shabu.
translations.idiomatic: Puguala reported that he could not tell how many Liao troops there were; the Founder was skeptical and sent Hu Shabu.

sentences.zh: 還報曰：「遼兵調兵，尚未大集。」

translations.literal: On his return he reported: "The Liao are mobilizing troops but have not yet gathered in force."
translations.idiomatic: He came back and reported, "The Liao are calling up troops but have not yet massed in strength."

sentences.zh: 及見統軍，使其孫被甲立於傍，統軍曰：「人謂汝輩且反，故為備耳。」

translations.literal: When he met the commander-in-chief, the commander had his grandson armored and standing at his side. The commander said, "People say you people are about to rebel, so we are on guard."
translations.idiomatic: When he met the frontier commander, the commander had his grandson stand beside him in armor. The commander said, "People say your people are plotting rebellion, so we have taken precautions."

sentences.zh: 及行道中，遇渤海軍，渤海軍向胡沙補且笑且言曰：「聞女直欲為亂，汝輩是邪。」

translations.literal: On the road he met Bohai troops, who laughed at Hu Shabu and said, "We hear the Jurchen mean to make trouble—is that you lot?"
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met Bohai soldiers, who laughed at Hu Shabu and said, "We hear the Jurchen are rising—is that you?"

sentences.zh: 具以告太祖，又曰：「今舉大事不可後時，若俟河凍，則遼兵盛集來攻矣。

translations.literal: He reported all this fully to the Founder and also said, "To undertake a great enterprise now one must not delay. If we wait until the rivers freeze, Liao troops will gather in strength and come to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He told the Founder everything and added, "We must not delay this great undertaking. If we wait until the rivers freeze, the Liao will mass their armies and strike.

sentences.zh: 乘其未集而早伐之，可以得志。」

translations.literal: Strike before they gather and one can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they are still scattered and we can prevail."

sentences.zh: 太祖深然之。

translations.literal: The Founder deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 及破甯江州，戰于達魯古城，皆有功，賜以旗鼓並禦器械。

translations.literal: When Ningjiang Prefecture was taken and they fought at Dalügu city, he had merit in both; he was granted banners, drums, and defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningjiang fell and they fought at Dalügu, he distinguished himself in both battles and was rewarded with banners, drums, and armor.

sentences.zh: 高永昌請和，胡沙補往招之，取胡突古以歸。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchang sought peace; Hu Shabu went to summon him and brought Hutugu back.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yongchang sued for peace, Hu Shabu went to win him over and brought Hutugu back with him.

sentences.zh: 高永昌詐降于斡魯，斡魯使胡沙補、撒八往報。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchang feigned surrender to Wolu; Wolu sent Hu Shabu and Sabo to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongchang pretended to submit to Wolu, who sent Hu Shabu and Sabo to confirm it.

sentences.zh: 會高楨降，言永昌非真降者，斡魯乃進兵。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhen surrendered, he said Yongchang's surrender was not genuine, and Wolu then advanced his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhen then surrendered and said Yongchang's submission was a sham, whereupon Wolu marched forward.

sentences.zh: 永昌怒，遂殺胡沙補，撒八，皆支解之。

translations.literal: Yongchang was enraged and thereupon killed Hu Shabu and Sabo, dismembering both.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yongchang killed Hu Shabu and Sabo and had both dismembered.

sentences.zh: 胡沙補就執，神色自若，罵永昌曰：「汝叛君逆天，今日殺我，明日及汝矣。」

translations.literal: When Hu Shabu was seized, his expression was calm. He cursed Yongchang: "You rebel against your lord and defy Heaven. Today you kill me; tomorrow it will reach you."
translations.idiomatic: Seized, Hu Shabu remained composed and cursed Yongchang: "You betray your sovereign and defy Heaven. Kill me today, and tomorrow the reckoning will be yours."

sentences.zh: 罵不絕口，至死。

translations.literal: He cursed without cease until death.
translations.idiomatic: He railed without stopping until he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十九。

translations.literal: He was fifty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 天會中，與撒八俱贈遙鎮節度使。

translations.literal: In the Tianhui era, he and Sabo were both posthumously made Military Commissioners of Yaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhui, he and Sabo were both posthumously appointed Military Commissioners of Yaozhen.

sentences.zh: 特虎，雅撻瀾水人。

translations.literal: Te Hu was a man of Yatalan River.
translations.idiomatic: Te Hu was from the Yatalan River region.

sentences.zh: 軀幹雄偉，敢戰鬥。

translations.literal: His frame was imposing and he was bold in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He had a powerful build and fought fearlessly.

sentences.zh: 達魯古城之役，活女陷敵，特虎救出之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Dalügu city, Huonü was trapped by the enemy; Te Hu rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalügu, Huonü was surrounded by the enemy; Te Hu fought his way in and brought him out.

sentences.zh: 攻照散城，遼兵三千來拒，特虎先登，敗之。

translations.literal: Attacking Zhaosan city, three thousand Liao troops came to resist; Te Hu was first to scale the wall and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When they assaulted Zhaosan, three thousand Liao troops barred the way; Te Hu was first over the wall and routed them.

sentences.zh: 攻盧葛營，麻吉墮馬，特虎獨殺遼兵數輩，掖而出之。

translations.literal: Attacking the Luge camp, Maji fell from his horse; Te Hu alone killed several Liao soldiers and supported him out.
translations.idiomatic: At the Luge camp, Maji was thrown from his horse; Te Hu cut down several Liao fighters single-handed and helped him to safety.

sentences.zh: 賞賚逾渥。

translations.literal: His rewards exceeded the norm.
translations.idiomatic: His rewards were exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 自臨潢班師，至遼河，餘睹來襲，婁室已引去，特虎獨殿，馬憊乃步鬥，婁室與數騎來救，特虎止曰：“我以一死捍敵，公勿來，俱毙无益。

translations.literal: Returning from Linhuang, at the Liao River, Yudu came to attack. Wushi had already withdrawn; Te Hu alone held the rear. His horse exhausted, he fought on foot. Wushi came with several horsemen to rescue him; Te Hu stopped them, saying, "I will hold the enemy with my death—do not come, sir; if we die together it profits nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Marching back from Linhuang, at the Liao River they were attacked by Yudu. Wushi had already pulled away; Te Hu alone covered the retreat. When his horse gave out he fought on foot. Wushi rode back with a few men to save him; Te Hu called out, "Let me hold them with my life—stay back, sir; if we all die here it helps no one."

sentences.zh: ”遂没於陣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 皇統間，贈明威將軍。

translations.literal: In the Huangtong era he was posthumously made General of Bright Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangtong he was posthumously made General of Bright Prestige.

sentences.zh: 僕忽得

translations.literal: Pu Hude
translations.idiomatic: Pu Hude

sentences.zh: 僕忽得，宗室子。

translations.literal: Pu Hude was a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Hude was of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 初事國相撒改，伐蕭海里有功。

translations.literal: He first served the State Chancellor Sagai and had merit in the campaign against Xiao Haili.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Chancellor Sagai and distinguished himself in the war against Xiao Haili.

sentences.zh: 與酬斡俱，招降燭偎水部族，酬斡為謀克，僕忽得領行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Together with Chouwo he subdued the Zhuwei River tribes; Chouwo became a commander (mouke), and Pu Hude led a thousand-household marching detachment.
translations.idiomatic: With Chouwo he brought the Zhuwei River tribes to submission; Chouwo was made a mouke commander while Pu Hude led a thousand-household field detachment.

sentences.zh: 從破黃龍府，戰于達魯古城，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Huanglong Prefecture and fought at Dalügu city, having merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the fall of Huanglong and the fight at Dalügu, earning credit in both.

sentences.zh: 甯江州渤海乙塞補叛，僕忽得追複之。

translations.literal: At Ningjiang, the Bohai Yisai Bu rebelled; Pu Hude pursued and recovered the place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bohai Yisai Bu rebelled at Ningjiang, Pu Hude pursued and retook the district.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年九月，酬斡、僕忽得往鱉古河籍軍馬，燭偎水部實里古達等七人殺酬斡、僕忽得，投其屍水中，俱年四十三。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Tianfu, Chouwo and Pu Hude went to the Biegu River to register troops and horses; Shiriguda and six others of the Zhuwei River tribe killed Chouwo and Pu Hude and threw their bodies into the water. Both were forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianfu 5, Chouwo and Pu Hude went to the Biegu River to muster horses and men; Shiriguda and six others of the Zhuwei River tribe killed them and cast their bodies into the river. Both were forty-three.

sentences.zh: 太祖悼惜，遣使吊賻加等。

translations.literal: The Founder mourned them and sent envoys with condolences and additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder grieved for them and sent envoys with condolences and extra gifts.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，斡魯伐實里古達于石里罕河，追及於合撻剌山，殺四人，撫定餘眾。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, Wolu attacked Shiriguda on the Shilihan River, overtook him at Hetala Mountain, killed four men, and pacified the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year six, Wolu campaigned against Shiriguda on the Shilihan, caught him at Hetala Mountain, executed four of the killers, and pacified the rest.

sentences.zh: 詔斡魯求酬斡、僕忽得屍以葬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wolu to seek the bodies of Chouwo and Pu Hude for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wolu was ordered to recover the bodies of Chouwo and Pu Hude for burial.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，贈酬斡奉國上將軍、僕忽得昭義大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianjuan era, Chouwo was posthumously made General Who Upholds the State and Pu Hude Grand General of Manifest Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianjuan, Chouwo was posthumously made General Who Upholds the State and Pu Hude Grand General of Manifest Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 酬斡，亦宗室子也。

translations.literal: Chouwo was also a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chouwo, too, was of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 年十五隸軍，從太祖伐遼，率濤溫路兵招撫三坦、石里很、跋苦三水鱉古城邑，皆降之。

translations.literal: At fifteen he entered the army and followed the Founder against Liao, leading Taowen Route troops to win over the towns of Santan, Shilihen, Bacu, and the three rivers' Biegu— all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he joined the army and followed the Founder against Liao, leading Taowen Route forces to bring in the settlements of Santan, Shilihen, Bacu, and the Biegu towns along the three rivers—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 敗室韋五百于阿良葛城，獲其民眾。

translations.literal: He defeated five hundred Shiwei at Aliange city and took their people.
translations.idiomatic: He routed five hundred Shiwei at Aliange and took their people captive.

sentences.zh: 至是死焉。

translations.literal: At this time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in this affair.

sentences.zh: 粘割韓奴

translations.literal: Nianhe Hannu
translations.idiomatic: Zhange Hannu

sentences.zh: 粘割韓奴，以護衛從宗弼征伐，賜鎧甲弓矢戰馬。

translations.literal: Nianhe Hannu, as a guardsman, followed Zongbi on campaigns and was granted armor, bow and arrows, and a war horse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhange Hannu served as a guardsman under Zongbi on campaign and was given armor, bow and arrows, and a war horse.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖入居庸關，遼林牙耶律大石自古北口亡去，以其眾來襲奉聖州，壁于龍門東二十五里，婁室往取之，獲大石並降其眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founder entered Juyong Pass, the Liao Grand Secretary Yelü Dashi fled through the northern pass with his followers, came with his force to attack Fengsheng Prefecture, and encamped twenty-five li east of Longmen. Wushi went to take him, captured Dashi, and received the surrender of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder first passed Juyong, the Liao Grand Secretary Yelü Dashi escaped through the northern pass with his men, struck at Fengsheng, and camped twenty-five li east of Longmen. Wushi marched against him, took Dashi prisoner, and accepted the surrender of his force.

sentences.zh: 宗望襲遼主輜重於青塚，以大石為鄉導，詔曰：「遼趙王習泥烈、林牙大石、北王喝里質、節度使訛里刺、孛堇赤狗兒、招討迪六、祥穩六斤、同知海里及諸官民，並釋其罪。」

translations.literal: Zongwang raided the Liao emperor's baggage train at Qingzhong, using Dashi as guide. An edict said: "The Liao Prince of Zhao Ximilie, Grand Secretary Dashi, Prince of the North Helizhi, Military Commissioner Elici, Commander Chigou'er, Pacification Commissioner Di Liu, Xiangwen Liujin, Vice Commissioner Haili, and all officials and people—their crimes are all remitted."
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang struck the Liao emperor's baggage train at Qingzhong with Dashi as guide. An edict declared: "The Liao Prince of Zhao Ximilie, Grand Secretary Dashi, Northern Prince Helizhi, Commissioner Elici, Commander Chigou'er, Pacification Commissioner Di Liu, Xiangwen Liujin, Vice Commissioner Haili, and all officials and commoners—their offenses are pardoned."

sentences.zh: 複詔斡魯曰：「林牙大石雖非降附，其為鄉導有勞，可明諭之。」

translations.literal: A further edict to Wolu said: "Although Grand Secretary Dashi did not truly submit, he has merit as a guide—this should be made clear to him."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict told Wolu, "Grand Secretary Dashi has not formally surrendered, but he has served well as a guide—make that plain to him."

sentences.zh: 時天輔六年也。

translations.literal: This was in the sixth year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: This was in Tianfu 6.

sentences.zh: 既而亡去，不知所往。

translations.literal: Afterward he fled away; no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled again, and no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，遼詳穩撻不野來降，言大石稱王於北方，署置南北面官僚，有戰馬萬匹，畜產甚眾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui, the Liao Xiangwen Tabuye came to surrender and said Dashi had declared himself king in the north, appointed officials for the northern and southern wings, had ten thousand war horses, and very many livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 2 the Liao Xiangwen Tabuye surrendered and reported that Dashi had proclaimed himself king in the north, set up northern and southern administrations, commanded ten thousand war horses, and held vast herds.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「追襲遼主，必酌事宜而行。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In pursuing the Liao emperor, one must act according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Pursuit of the Liao emperor must follow what circumstances allow.

sentences.zh: 攻討大石，須俟報下。」

translations.literal: Attacking Dashi must await further orders."
translations.idiomatic: Striking at Dashi must wait for further orders."

sentences.zh: 三年，都统完顏希尹言，聞夏人與耶律大石約曰：「大金既獲遼主，諸軍皆將歸矣，宜合兵以取山西諸部。」

translations.literal: In the third year, Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Xiyin reported hearing that the Xia and Yelü Dashi had agreed: "The Great Jin has captured the Liao emperor and all armies will soon return; we should combine forces to take the western Shanxi tribes."
translations.idiomatic: In year three, Commander Wanyan Xiyin reported that the Xia and Yelü Dashi had agreed: "Now that the Jin hold the Liao emperor, their armies will soon withdraw—we should join forces and seize the western tribes."

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「夏人或與大石合謀為釁，不可不察，其嚴備之。」

translations.literal: The edict replied: "The Xia may be plotting trouble with Dashi; this cannot go unexamined—make strict preparations."
translations.idiomatic: The court answered, "The Xia may be scheming with Dashi—do not neglect it; strengthen your defenses."

sentences.zh: 七年，泰州路都統婆盧火奏：「大石已得北部二營，恐後難制，且近群牧，宜列屯戍。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Taizhou Route Commander-in-Chief Poluhuo memorialized: "Dashi has taken two northern camps; he may be hard to control later, and he is near the herd pastures—garrisons should be posted."
translations.idiomatic: In year seven, Taizhou Route commander Poluhuo reported: "Dashi has seized two northern camps; he may grow unmanageable, and he is close to our pastures—station troops there."

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「以二營之故發兵，諸部必擾，當謹斥候而已。」

translations.literal: The edict replied: "To send troops for two camps would surely disturb the tribes; one should only keep careful watch."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "Mobilizing over two camps would unsettle the tribes—maintain vigilant scouts only."

sentences.zh: 八年，遣耶律余睹、石家奴、拔離速追討大石，徵兵諸部，諸部不從，石家奴至兀納水而還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yelü Yudu, Shijianu, and Balisu were sent to pursue Dashi; when troops were levied from the tribes they would not obey, and Shijianu reached the Wuna River and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, Yelü Yudu, Shijianu, and Balisu were dispatched against Dashi; the tribes refused the levy, and Shijianu turned back at the Wuna River.

sentences.zh: 余睹報元帥府曰：「聞耶律大石在和州之域，恐與夏人合，當遣使索之。」

translations.literal: Yudu reported to the Marshal's Office: "I hear Yelü Dashi is in the Hezhou region; I fear he may join with the Xia—envoys should be sent to demand him."
translations.idiomatic: Yudu reported to headquarters: "Dashi is said to be in the Hezhou region; he may ally with the Xia—send envoys to demand his surrender."

sentences.zh: 夏國報曰：「小國與和州壤地不相接，且不知大石所往也。」

translations.literal: The Xia state replied: "Our small state does not border the Hezhou lands, and we do not know where Dashi has gone either."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia answered, "Our realm does not adjoin Hezhou, and we do not know Dashi's whereabouts either."

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，回紇遣使入貢，言大石與其國相鄰，大石已死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong, the Uighurs sent tribute envoys saying Dashi bordered their state and that Dashi was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 4, Uighur envoys came with tribute and said Dashi's realm bordered theirs and that Dashi was already dead.

sentences.zh: 詔遣韓奴與其使俱往，因觀其國風俗，加武義將軍，奉使大石。

translations.literal: An edict sent Hannu with their envoys, to observe the customs of that country; he was promoted to General of Martial Righteousness and commissioned as envoy to Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: Hannu was ordered to go with the envoys to observe their customs; he was made General of Martial Righteousness and sent as envoy to Dashi.

sentences.zh: 韓奴去後不復聞問。

translations.literal: After Hannu departed, no further word was heard.
translations.idiomatic: After Hannu left, nothing more was heard of him.

sentences.zh: 大定中，回紇移習覽三人至西南招討司貿易，自言：「本國回紇鄒括番部，所居城名骨斯訛魯朵，俗無兵器，以田為業，所獲十分之一輸官。

translations.literal: In the Dading era, three Uighur Yixilan came to the Southwest Pacification Commission to trade and said of themselves: "Our state's Uighur Zoukuo tribe dwells in a city called Gusi Woluduo; by custom they have no weapons, take farming as their occupation, and pay one-tenth of the harvest to the government.
translations.idiomatic: During Dading, three Uighur traders named Yixilan came to the Southwest Pacification Commission and said: "We are of the Uighur Zoukuo tribe; our capital is called Gusi Woluduo. We keep no arms, live by farming, and pay a tenth of the harvest to our rulers.

sentences.zh: 耆老相傳，先時契丹至不能拒，因臣之。

translations.literal: The elders transmit that formerly, when the Khitan came, they could not resist and therefore became subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Elders say that when the Khitan first came they could not resist and submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 契丹所居屯營，乘馬行自旦至日中始周匝。

translations.literal: The Khitan encampment, riding around it from dawn until midday, is only then circled.
translations.idiomatic: Riding around the Khitan camp takes from dawn until noon.

sentences.zh: 近歲契丹使其女婿阿本斯領兵五萬北攻葉不輦等部族，不克而還，至今相攻未已。」

translations.literal: In recent years the Khitan sent their son-in-law Abensi to lead fifty thousand troops north to attack the Yebulian and other tribes; he did not succeed and returned, and fighting continues to this day."
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Khitan sent their son-in-law Abensi north with fifty thousand men against the Yebulian and other tribes; he failed and withdrew, and raids continue to this day."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此人非隸朝廷番部，不鬚髮遣，可于咸平府舊有回紇人中安置，毋令失所。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "These men are not tribes subject to the court; they need not be sent back. They may be settled among the former Uighurs at Xianping Prefecture so they do not lose their livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled: "They are not subjects of our border tribes and need not be sent home. Settle them among the Uighurs already at Xianping so they are not left destitute."

sentences.zh: 是歲，粘拔恩君長撒里雅寅特斯率康里部長孛古及戶三萬餘求內附，乞納前大石所降牌印，受朝廷牌印。

translations.literal: That year, the Zhaba'en chieftain Saliyayintesi led the Kangli chief Bugu and more than thirty thousand households to seek inner submission, asking to surrender the tallies formerly given by Dashi and receive court tallies.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Zhaba'en chief Saliyayintesi led Kangli chief Bugu and over thirty thousand households to submit, offering to hand back the seals Dashi had given them and receive imperial seals instead.

sentences.zh: 詔西南招討司遣人慰問，且觀其意。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Southwest Pacification Commission to send men to console them and observe their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The Southwest Pacification Commission was told to send envoys to welcome them and gauge their intentions.

sentences.zh: 禿里餘睹、通事阿魯帶至其國見撒里雅，具言願歸朝廷，乞降牌印，無他意也。

translations.literal: Tuli Yudu and interpreter Aludai went to their country, met Saliya, and stated fully their wish to return to the court, begging to surrender tallies and having no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli Yudu and interpreter Aludai visited Saliya and reported that they wished to submit to the court, sought to hand over their seals, and had no ulterior motive.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「往年大國嘗遣粘割韓奴自和州往使大石，既入其境，大石方適野，與韓奴相遇，問韓奴何人敢不下馬，韓奴曰：' 我上國使也，奉天子之命來招汝降，汝當下馬聽詔。

translations.literal: They then said: "In former years the great state once sent Nianhe Hannu from Hezhou as envoy to Dashi. Once he entered their territory, Dashi happened to be out hunting and met Hannu. He asked who Hannu was to dare not dismount. Hannu said, 'I am an envoy of the superior state, sent by the Son of Heaven to summon your surrender—you should dismount and hear the edict.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "Years ago the great state sent Zhange Hannu from Hezhou to Dashi. Hannu entered their land while Dashi was hunting. Dashi asked who he was to ride without dismounting. Hannu replied, 'I am an envoy of the Son of Heaven, sent to demand your surrender—you should dismount and hear the decree.

sentences.zh: '大石曰：'汝單使來，欲事口舌耶？

translations.literal: Dashi said, 'You come alone—do you mean to rely on words?
translations.idiomatic: Dashi said, "You come alone—do you think talk will suffice?"

sentences.zh: '使人捽下，使韓奴跪，韓奴罵曰：'反賊，天子不忍于爾加兵，遣招汝。

translations.literal: His men seized him and forced Hannu to kneel. Hannu cursed: 'Rebel! The Son of Heaven could not bear to send troops against you and dispatched me to summon you.
translations.idiomatic: His men seized Hannu and forced him to his knees. Hannu cursed, "Traitor! The Son of Heaven spared you the sword and sent me to summon you."

sentences.zh: 爾縱不能面縛請罪闕下，亦當盡敬天子之使，乃敢反加辱乎！

translations.literal: Even if you cannot bind yourself and beg pardon at the court, you should still show full respect to the Son of Heaven's envoy—how dare you instead add insult!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you will not bind yourself and plead guilty at court, you should honor the Son of Heaven's envoy—how dare you insult him instead!

sentences.zh: '大石怒，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Dashi was enraged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Dashi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 此時大石林牙已死，子孫相繼，西方諸部仍以大石呼之。

translations.literal: By this time the Great Liao Linya Dashi was already dead; descendants succeeded one another, and the western tribes still called him by the name Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Great Liao prince Dashi was dead and his line had succeeded him, but the western tribes still spoke of him as Dashi.

sentences.zh: '」余睹、阿魯帶還奏，並奏韓奴事。

translations.literal: Yudu and Aludai returned and reported, also reporting Hannu's affair."
translations.idiomatic: Yudu and Aludai returned and reported this, including Hannu's fate."

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉韓奴忠節，贈昭毅大將軍，召其子永和縣商酒都監詳古、汝州巡檢婁室諭之曰：「汝父奉使萬里，不辱君命，能盡死節，朕甚閔之。」

translations.literal: The Shizong praised Hannu's loyal integrity, posthumously made him Grand General of Bright Resolution, and summoned his sons Xianggu, Superintendent of Wine Trade at Yonghe County, and Wushi, Ruzhou Inspector, telling them: "Your father went on mission ten thousand li, did not disgrace his lord's command, and could die to the full measure of integrity—I deeply pity him."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong honored Hannu's loyalty, posthumously made him Grand General of Bright Resolution, and summoned his sons Xianggu, wine superintendent at Yonghe, and Wushi, inspector at Ruzhou, saying, "Your father traveled ten thousand li on embassy, upheld his sovereign's charge, and died faithful to the end—I grieve for him deeply."

sentences.zh: 詳古為尚輦局直長，遷武義將軍，婁室為武器署直長。

translations.literal: Xianggu became a direct attendant in the Imperial Carriage Office and was transferred to General of Martial Righteousness; Wushi became a direct attendant in the Weapons Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggu was made an attendant in the Imperial Carriage Office and promoted to General of Martial Righteousness; Wushi was appointed to the Weapons Office.

sentences.zh: 曹珪，徐州人。

translations.literal: Cao Gui was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gui was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，州人江志作亂，珪子弼在賊黨中，珪謀誅志，並弼殺之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, the townsman Jiang Zhi rebelled; Gui's son Bi was among the rebels. Gui plotted to kill Zhi and killed Bi together with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 4 the townsman Jiang Zhi rose in revolt; Gui's son Bi was among the rebels. Gui plotted to kill Zhi and slew Bi along with him.

sentences.zh: 尚書省議，當補二官雜班敘。

translations.literal: The Secretariat deliberated that he should be given two ranks in the miscellaneous roster.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat proposed promoting him two ranks on the miscellaneous roster.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「圭赤心為國，大義滅親，自古罕聞也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Gui's loyal heart was for the state; he extinguished kin for righteousness—rarely heard of since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Gui served the state with a loyal heart and sacrificed kin for righteousness—seldom seen in any age.

sentences.zh: 法雖如是，然未足以當其功，更進一官，正班用之。」

translations.literal: Though the law is thus, it is not enough for his merit; advance him one more rank and employ him in the regular roster."
translations.idiomatic: The law would not suffice for his merit; promote him one further rank and appoint him on the regular roster."

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕蒲睹

translations.literal: Wendihan Pudu
translations.idiomatic: Wendihanpudu

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕蒲睹，為兀者群牧使。

translations.literal: Wendihan Pudu was Superintendent of the Wuzhe Herd Pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihanpudu was superintendent of the Wuzhe herd pastures.

sentences.zh: 西北路契丹撒八等反，諸群牧皆應之。

translations.literal: On the Northwest Route the Khitan Saba and others rebelled, and all the herd superintendencies responded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Saba rebelled on the Northwest Route, every herd superintendent joined them.

sentences.zh: 蒲睹聞亂作，選家奴材勇者數十人，給以兵仗，陰為之備。

translations.literal: When Pudu heard rebellion had broken out, he selected several dozen household slaves who were brave and capable, gave them weapons, and secretly prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt, Pudu picked several dozen brave household slaves, armed them, and made secret preparations.

sentences.zh: 賊不得發，乃紿諸奴曰：「官閱兵器，願借兵仗以應閱。」

translations.literal: The rebels could not act, so he deceived the slaves, saying, "Officials are inspecting weapons; I wish to borrow arms to meet the inspection."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could not strike, so he tricked the slaves: "Officials are inspecting arms—I need to borrow your weapons for the review."

sentences.zh: 諸奴以為實然，遂借與之。

translations.literal: The slaves thought it genuine and lent them to him.
translations.idiomatic: The slaves believed him and handed over their weapons.

sentences.zh: 明旦，賊至，蒲睹無以禦之。

translations.literal: At dawn the rebels came; Pudu had no means to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels arrived, and Pudu had nothing with which to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 賊執蒲睹而問之曰：「今欲反未？」

translations.literal: The rebels seized Pudu and asked him: "Do you wish to rebel now?"
translations.idiomatic: They seized Pudu and asked, "Will you join the rebellion now?"

sentences.zh: 蒲睹曰：「吾家世受國厚恩，子侄皆仕宦，不能從汝反而累吾族也。」

translations.literal: Pudu said: "My family for generations has received the state's deep favor; my sons and nephews all hold office—I cannot follow you in rebellion and bring ruin on my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Pudu replied, "My family has enjoyed the state's bounty for generations; my sons and nephews all serve in office. I cannot rebel with you and destroy my whole clan."

sentences.zh: 賊怒，臠而殺之，子與孫皆與害。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged, dismembered and killed him, and his sons and grandsons perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels dismembered and killed him, and his sons and grandsons died as well.

sentences.zh: 是時，迪斡群牧使徒單賽里、副使赤盞胡失答，耶魯瓦群牧使鶴壽，歐里不群牧使完顏朮里骨、副使完顏辭不失，卜迪不部副使赤盞胡失賴，速木典颭詳穩加古買住，胡睹颭詳穩完顏速沒葛，轄木颭詳穩高彭祖等皆遇害。

translations.literal: At this time, the Diwo Herd Superintendent Tushan Saili and Vice Superintendent Chizan Hushida, the Yeluwa Herd Superintendent Heshou, the Oulibu Herd Superintendent Wanyan Zhuligu and Vice Superintendent Wanyan Cibushi, the Budibu Vice Superintendent Chizan Hushilai, the Sumudian Xiangwen Jiagu Maizhu, the Hudu Xiangwen Wanyan Sumoge, the Xiamu Xiangwen Gao Pengzu, and others all met harm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Diwo herd superintendent Tushan Saili and vice superintendent Chizan Hushida, Yeluwa superintendent Heshou, Oulibu superintendent Wanyan Zhuligu and vice superintendent Wanyan Cibushi, Budibu vice superintendent Chizan Hushilai, Sumudian xiangwen Jiagu Maizhu, Hudu xiangwen Wanyan Sumoge, Xiamu xiangwen Gao Pengzu, and others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 鶴壽，鄆王昂子，本名吾都不。

translations.literal: Heshou was a son of Prince Yun of Yan, original name Wudubu.
translations.idiomatic: Heshou was a son of Prince Yun of Yan; his original name was Wudubu.

sentences.zh: 五院部人老和尚率眾來招鶴壽與俱反，鶴壽曰：「吾宗室子，受國厚恩，寧殺我，不能與賊俱反。」

translations.literal: Laoheshang of the Five Courts Department led his followers to summon Heshou to rebel with them. Heshou said: "I am of the imperial clan and have received the state's deep favor—better kill me than join rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Laoheshang of the Five Courts led men to urge Heshou to rebel with them. Heshou said, "I am of the imperial clan and owe the state a great debt—kill me if you will, but I will not join rebels."

sentences.zh: 遂與二子皆被殺。

translations.literal: He and his two sons were then all killed.
translations.idiomatic: He and his two sons were then slain.

sentences.zh: 訛里也

translations.literal: E Liye
translations.idiomatic: E Liye

sentences.zh: 訛里也，契丹人。

translations.literal: E Liye was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: E Liye was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 為尚廄局直長。

translations.literal: He was a direct attendant in the Imperial Stables Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a direct attendant in the Imperial Stables Office.

sentences.zh: 大定初，招諭契丹，窩斡叱令訛里也跪見，訛里也不從，謂曰：「我朝廷使也，豈可屈節於汝。

translations.literal: In early Dading, while winning over the Khitan, Wowo ordered E Liye to kneel and appear before him; E Liye would not obey and said: "I am an envoy of the court—how can I bow to you?
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading, during pacification of the Khitan, Wowo ordered E Liye to kneel before him. E Liye refused: "I am a court envoy—how can I bow to you?

sentences.zh: 汝等早降可全性命，若大軍至，汝輩悔將何及。」

translations.literal: If you submit early you may preserve your lives; when the great army arrives, what use will your regret be?"
translations.idiomatic: Surrender now and you may live; when the imperial army comes, regret will be too late."

sentences.zh: 窩斡怒曰：「汝本契丹人，而不我從，敢出是言。」

translations.literal: Wowo angrily said: "You are originally a Khitan yet will not follow me—how dare you speak thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Wowo raged: "You are a Khitan yourself, yet you refuse to follow me—how dare you say such things!"

sentences.zh: 遂害之。

translations.literal: He then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had him killed.

sentences.zh: 從行驍騎軍士閏孫、史大、習馬小底頗答皆被害。

translations.literal: The accompanying elite cavalry soldiers Runsun, Shi Da, and horse-handler Poda were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The elite cavalrymen Runsun and Shi Da and the horse-handler Poda who accompanied him were all killed.

sentences.zh: 三年，贈訛里也宣武將軍，錄其子阿不沙為外帳小底。

translations.literal: In the third year, E Liye was posthumously made General of Manifest Martiality and his son Abusha was enrolled as an outer-account attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year three E Liye was posthumously made General of Manifest Martiality and his son Abusha was appointed an outer-account attendant.

sentences.zh: 閏孫、史大皆贈修武校尉。

translations.literal: Runsun and Shi Da were both posthumously made Rectifier of Martiality Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Runsun and Shi Da were both posthumously made Rectifier of Martiality commandants.

sentences.zh: 頗答贈忠翊校尉。

translations.literal: Poda was posthumously made Loyal Assistant Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Poda was posthumously made Loyal Assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 納蘭綽赤

translations.literal: Nalan Chaochi
translations.idiomatic: Nalan Chaochi

sentences.zh: 納蘭綽赤，咸平路伊改河猛安人。

translations.literal: Nalan Chaochi was a man of the Yigai River Military Colony on Xianping Route.
translations.idiomatic: Nalan Chaochi was from the Yigai River military colony in Xianping circuit.

sentences.zh: 契丹括里使人招之，綽赤不從。

translations.literal: The Khitan Kuoli sent men to summon him; Chaochi would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leader Kuoli sent envoys to recruit him, but Chaochi refused.

sentences.zh: 括里兵且至，綽赤遂團結旁近村寨為兵，出家馬百餘匹給之，教以戰陣擊刺之法，相與拒括里于伊改渡口，由是賊眾月餘不得進。

translations.literal: When Kuoli's troops were about to arrive, Chaochi rallied nearby villages and hamlets as soldiers, gave out more than a hundred household horses, taught them battle formations and thrusting techniques, and together resisted Kuoli at the Yigai River ford; thus the rebels for more than a month could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: As Kuoli's army approached, Chaochi rallied neighboring villages, supplied more than a hundred household horses, trained them in formation and spear work, and held the Yigai ford against Kuoli for over a month.

sentences.zh: 既而括里兵四萬人大至，綽赤拒戰，賊兵十倍，遂見執，臠而殺之。

translations.literal: Then Kuoli's forty thousand troops arrived in force; Chaochi resisted, but the rebels were ten times his strength; he was seized and dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuoli arrived with forty thousand men, Chaochi fought on though outnumbered ten to one, was captured, and dismembered.

sentences.zh: 詔贈官兩階，二子皆得用廕。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously advanced him two ranks; both sons received hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted two ranks, and both sons received hereditary appointment.

sentences.zh: 魏全，壽州人。

translations.literal: Wei Quan was a native of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Quan was from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，宋李爽圍壽州，刺史徒單羲盡籍城中兵民及部曲廝役得三千餘人，隨機拒守堅甚。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, the Song general Li Shuang besieged Shouzhou; Prefect Tushan Yi mustered all soldiers and civilians in the city plus retainers and servants, obtaining more than three thousand men, and defended flexibly with great firmness.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 the Song general Li Shuang besieged Shouzhou. Prefect Tushan Yi enrolled every soldier, civilian, retainer, and servant in the city—more than three thousand in all—and mounted a stubborn, resourceful defense.

sentences.zh: 羲善撫禦，得眾情，雖婦人皆樂為用。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled in comforting and controlling the people and won their hearts; even women were glad to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Yi won the people's loyalty through firm but humane leadership; even the women were eager to help.

sentences.zh: 同知蒲烈古中流矢卒，羲益勵不衰，募人往斫爽營，全在選中，為爽兵所執。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Puliegu died of an arrow wound; Yi redoubled his efforts without slackening, recruited men to raid Shuang's camp, and Quan was chosen but seized by Shuang's troops.
translations.idiomatic: When vice commissioner Puliegu fell to an arrow, Yi only fought harder. He recruited men to raid Shuang's camp; Quan was chosen and captured by Song troops.

sentences.zh: 爽謂全曰：「若為我罵金主，免若死。」

translations.literal: Shuang said to Quan: "If you curse the Jin emperor for me, I will spare your life."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang told Quan, "Curse the Jin emperor for me and I will spare you."

sentences.zh: 全至城下，反罵宋主，爽乃殺之，至死罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Quan came beneath the wall and instead cursed the Song emperor; Shuang then killed him, and he cursed without cease until death.
translations.idiomatic: At the wall Quan cursed the Song emperor instead; Shuang killed him, but Quan railed without stopping until he died.

sentences.zh: 僕散揆遣河南統軍判官乞住及買哥等以騎二千人救壽州，去壽州十餘里與爽兵遇，乞住分兩翼夾擊爽兵，大破之，斬首萬餘級，追奔至城下，拔其三柵，焚其浮梁。

translations.literal: Pusan Huai sent Henan Commander-in-Chief's Judge Qizhu and Maige and others with two thousand horsemen to relieve Shouzhou. More than ten li from Shouzhou they met Shuang's troops; Qizhu divided into two wings and struck Shuang's army from both sides, routing them greatly, beheading more than ten thousand, pursuing to the walls, taking three stockades, and burning their pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Huai sent Henan commander judge Qizhu and Maige with two thousand cavalry to relieve Shouzhou. Ten li out they met Shuang's force; Qizhu split his wings and crushed them, taking more than ten thousand heads, driving them to the walls, capturing three stockades, and burning their pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 羲出兵應之，爽兵大潰，赴淮死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Yi led troops out to meet them; Shuang's army collapsed in great disorder, and many died drowning in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sallied out to join the attack; Shuang's army broke and many drowned in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 爽與其副田林僅脫身去，餘兵脫者十之四。

translations.literal: Shuang and his lieutenant Tian Lin barely escaped; of the rest only four in ten got away.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang and his deputy Tian Lin barely escaped; only four tenths of their men survived.

sentences.zh: 詔遷羲防禦使、乞住同知昌武軍節度使事、買哥河南路統軍判官。

translations.literal: An edict transferred Yi to Defense Commissioner, Qizhu to Vice Commissioner of Changwu Military Commission, and Maige to Judge of Henan Route Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was made defense commissioner, Qizhu vice commissioner of Changwu, and Maige judge on the Henan command staff.

sentences.zh: 贈蒲烈古昭勇大將軍，官其子圖剌。

translations.literal: Puliegu was posthumously made Grand General of Manifest Valor and his son Tula was given office.
translations.idiomatic: Puliegu was posthumously made Grand General of Manifest Valor and his son Tula was given an appointment.

sentences.zh: 贈全宣武將軍、蒙城縣令，封其妻為鄉君，賜在州官舍三間、錢百萬，俟其子年至十五歲收充八貫石正班局分承應，用所贈官廕，仍以全死節送史館，鏤版頒諭天下。

translations.literal: Quan was posthumously made General of Manifest Martiality and Magistrate of Mengcheng County; his wife was enfeoffed as District Lady; three rooms of official lodging in the prefecture and a million cash were granted; when his son reached fifteen he was to be enrolled as a regular-rank attendant of the Eight-Guan-Shi bureau, using the posthumous rank's hereditary privilege; Quan's loyal death was sent to the Historiography Office and carved on plates promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was posthumously made General of Manifest Martiality and magistrate of Mengcheng; his wife was made a district lady; three official rooms in the prefecture and a million cash were granted; at fifteen his son would enter service on the regular roster using Quan's posthumous rank; Quan's death for the state was recorded in the Historiography Office and proclaimed nationwide on engraved placards.

sentences.zh: 執中死，詔削官爵。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong died, an edict stripped his offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhizhong's death his titles were revoked by edict.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「宣武將軍、護衛十人長完顏石古乃，修武校尉、符寶祗候鄯陽，忠孝勇果，沒于王事。

translations.literal: An edict said: "General of Manifest Martiality and Ten-Man Guards Captain Wanyan Shigu'nai, and Rectifier of Martiality Commandant and Talisman Attendant Shanyang—loyal, filial, brave, and resolute—died in the king's service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "General of Manifest Martiality and guards captain Wanyan Shigu'nai, and Rectifier of Martiality commandant and talisman attendant Shanyang—loyal, filial, brave, and steadfast—died in the emperor's service.

sentences.zh: 石古乃贈鎮國上將軍、順州刺史，鄯陽贈宣武將軍、順天軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Shigu'nai was posthumously made General Who Stabilizes the State and Prefect of Shunzhou; Shanyang was posthumously made General of Manifest Martiality and Vice Commissioner of Shuntian Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu'nai was posthumously made General Who Stabilizes the State and prefect of Shunzhou; Shanyang was made General of Manifest Martiality and vice commissioner of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 嘗從拒戰猛安賞錢五百貫、謀克三百貫、蒲輦散軍二百貫，各遷兩階。

translations.literal: Those who had followed in resisting battle: military colonels were rewarded five hundred strings of cash, commanders three hundred, and Pulian irregulars two hundred; each was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had fought in the defense were rewarded—colonels five hundred strings, commanders three hundred, irregulars two hundred—and each was promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 戰沒者，贈賞付其家。

translations.literal: Those who died in battle received posthumous rewards paid to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous rewards were paid to the families of those killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 石古乃子尚幼，以八貫石俸給之，俟年十五以聞。

translations.literal: Shigu'nai's son was still young; he was given Eight-Guan-Shi stipend until he reached fifteen, when it was to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu'nai's son was still young and was given an Eight-Guan-Shi stipend until he turned fifteen, when the court would be notified.

sentences.zh: 夾穀守中

translations.literal: Jiagu Shouzhong
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu Shouzhong

sentences.zh: 夾穀守中，咸平人，本名阿土古。

translations.literal: Jiagu Shouzhong was a native of Xianping, original name Atugu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagu Shouzhong was from Xianping; his original name was Atugu.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年進士，曆清池、聞喜主簿，補尚書省令史，除刑部主事、監察禦史、修起居注。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-second year of Dading, he served as registrar of Qingchi and Wenxi, was appointed Secretariat clerk, and was made Principal Clerk of the Ministry of Justice, Investigating Censor, and Compiler of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Dading 22, served as registrar at Qingchi and Wenxi, became a Secretariat clerk, and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, investigating censor, and compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 轉禮部員外郎、大名治中，曆嵩琢、北京、臨洮路按察副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Daming Administrator, and served as Vice Surveillance Commissioner on Songzhuo, Bejing, and Lintao routes.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of the Ministry of Rites and administrator of Daming, then served as vice surveillance commissioner on the Songzhuo, Bejing, and Lintao circuits.

sentences.zh: 以憂去官，起複同知曷懶路兵馬都總管府事，坐事謫韓州刺史，尋複同知平涼府事。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning, was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Yilan Route Military Command, was demoted to Prefect of Hanzhou for an offense, and soon restored as Vice Commissioner of Pingliang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for mourning, returned as vice commissioner of the Yilan military command, was demoted to prefect of Hanzhou for an offense, and soon restored as vice commissioner of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 大安二年，為秦州防禦使，遷通遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Da'an he was Defense Commissioner of Qinzhou and was transferred to Military Commissioner of Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an 2 he was defense commissioner of Qinzhou, then military commissioner of Tongyuan.

sentences.zh: 至寧末，移彰化軍，未行，夏兵數萬入鞏州。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhi'ning he was to transfer to Zhanghua Army but had not yet departed when tens of thousands of Xia troops entered Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhi'ning he was ordered to Zhanghua but had not yet left when tens of thousands of Xia troops invaded Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 守中乘城備守，兵少不能支，城陷，官吏盡降，守中獨不屈。

translations.literal: Shouzhong manned the walls to defend; troops were few and could not hold; the city fell and all officials surrendered—only Shouzhong would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong defended the walls, but his few troops could not hold; the city fell and every official surrendered except Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 夏人壯之，且誘且脅，守中益堅，遂載而西。

translations.literal: The Xia admired him and both tempted and coerced him; Shouzhong grew firmer and was then carried west.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia admired his spirit and tried both persuasion and threats; Shouzhong only grew more resolute, and they carried him west.

sentences.zh: 至平涼，要以招降府人，守中佯許，至城下即大呼曰：「外兵矢盡且遁矣，慎勿降。」

translations.literal: At Pingliang they required him to win over the prefectural people to surrender; Shouzhong pretended to agree, but at the foot of the wall he shouted: "The outer troops' arrows are spent and they are fleeing—take care not to surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang they forced him to induce the city to surrender. He feigned agreement, but at the wall he shouted, "The enemy are out of arrows and fleeing—do not surrender!"

sentences.zh: 夏人交刃殺之。

translations.literal: The Xia crossed blades and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia cut him down with their blades.

sentences.zh: 石抹元毅

translations.literal: Shimo Yuanyi
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Yuanyi

sentences.zh: 石抹元毅，本名神思，咸平府路酌赤烈猛安莎果歌仙謀克人也。

translations.literal: Shimo Yuanyi, original name Shensi, was a man of the Zhuochilie Military Colony Shaguogexian Mouke on Xianping Prefecture Route.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Yuanyi, born Shensi, was from the Shaguogexian mouke of the Zhuochilie colony on the Xianping circuit.

sentences.zh: 以廕補吏部令史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by hereditary privilege as a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 再調景州寧津令，有劇盜白晝恣劫為民害，元毅以術防捍，賊散去。

translations.literal: Transferred again as Magistrate of Ningjin in Jingzhou, when fierce bandits plundered by day and harmed the people, Yuanyi used stratagems to defend against them and the bandits dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned as magistrate of Ningjin in Jingzhou, he drove off daylight bandits who had been terrorizing the people by shrewd defensive measures.

sentences.zh: 入為大理知法，除同知亳州防禦使事，被省檄，錄陝右五路刑獄，無冤人。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as legal specialist of the Court of Judicial Review, was made Vice Commissioner of Bozhou Defense, received a provincial commission to review criminal cases in the five western Shaanxi routes, and found no wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: He became a legal specialist at the Court of Judicial Review, then vice commissioner of Bozhou defense; commissioned to review criminal cases in the five western Shaanxi circuits, he found no wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 複委受宋歲幣，故事有私遺物，元毅一無所受。

translations.literal: He was again entrusted to receive the Song annual tribute; by precedent there were private gifts, but Yuanyi accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He was again assigned to receive the Song annual tribute; though custom allowed private gifts, he accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，驛召為大名等路提刑判官，以最遷汾陽軍節度副使。

translations.literal: In early Mingchang he was summoned by post as Criminal Judge on Daming and other routes, and for excellence was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Fenyang Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Mingchang he was summoned by courier as criminal judge on the Daming circuit and, for outstanding service, made vice commissioner of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 時石、嵐間賊黨嘯聚，肆行剽掠，朝廷命元毅捕之，賊畏而遁。

translations.literal: At that time bandit gangs gathered between Shi and Lan and plundered freely; the court ordered Yuanyi to capture them, and the bandits fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were raiding between Shi and Lan; ordered to suppress them, Yuanyi frightened them into flight.

sentences.zh: 元毅追襲，盡殪之，二境以安。

translations.literal: Yuanyi pursued and killed them all, and the two regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and destroyed them, pacifying both districts.

sentences.zh: 遷同知武勝軍節度使事，別郡有殺人者，屢鞫不伏，元毅訊不數語，即具服。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Commissioner of Wusheng Military Commission; in another prefecture a murderer had been interrogated repeatedly without confessing—Yuanyi questioned him in a few words and he fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Made vice commissioner of Wusheng, he took over a murder case another prefecture had failed to break; after a few questions the killer confessed fully.

sentences.zh: 河東北路田多山阪磽瘠，大比時定為上賦，民力久困，朝廷命相地更賦，元毅以三壤法平之，民賴其利。

translations.literal: On Hedong North Route much land was hilly, stony, and poor; at the great assessment it had been fixed as top-grade tax and the people's strength had long been strained. The court ordered land to be surveyed and taxes reassessed; Yuanyi balanced them by the three-soil method and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Much land on the Hedong North circuit was barren hills rated top-grade at the great survey, crushing the people. Ordered to reassess taxes by soil quality, Yuanyi applied the three-grade method and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 改彰德府治中，尋以邊警授撫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Administrator of Zhangde Prefecture, and soon because of border alarms was made Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became administrator of Zhangde, then prefect of Fuzhou when border alarms arose.

sentences.zh: 會邊將失守，芻糧馬牛焚剽殆盡，元毅率吏卒三十餘人出州經畫軍餉，卒與敵遇。

translations.literal: When frontier generals lost their posts, fodder, grain, horses, and cattle were burned and plundered nearly to extinction; Yuanyi led more than thirty clerks and soldiers out of the prefecture to arrange military supplies and suddenly met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier commanders failed, fodder and livestock were burned or looted almost to nothing; Yuanyi led thirty-odd clerks and soldiers out to gather supplies and ran into the enemy.

sentences.zh: 州倅暨從吏堅請還，元毅曰：「我輩責任邊守，遇敵而奔，其如百姓何？

translations.literal: The vice prefect and attending clerks urgently begged to return; Yuanyi said: "Our duty is to guard the border—if we flee at meeting the enemy, what of the common people?
translations.idiomatic: The vice prefect and his men begged to retreat. Yuanyi said, "We are charged with guarding the border—if we flee, what becomes of the people?

sentences.zh: 縱得自安，複何面目見朝廷乎！」

translations.literal: Even if we save ourselves, how could we face the court again!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if we saved ourselves, how could we face the court again!"

sentences.zh: 遂執弓矢令眾。

translations.literal: He then took bow and arrows and commanded the group.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his bow and took command.

sentences.zh: 眾感其忠，爭為效死。

translations.literal: The men were moved by his loyalty and vied to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his loyalty, they vied to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 元毅力戰，射無不中。

translations.literal: Yuanyi fought fiercely; every shot hit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi fought fiercely and never missed his mark.

sentences.zh: 敵去而複合，元毅氣愈厲，鏖戰久之，眾寡不敵，遂遇害，時年四十七。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew and regrouped; Yuanyi's spirit grew fiercer; after long bitter fighting, outnumbered, he met harm—he was forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew and returned; Yuanyi fought on with growing fury until, overwhelmed by numbers, he was killed at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上深驚悼，贈信武將軍，召用其子世勣侍儀司承應。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor was deeply shocked and mourned; Yuanyi was posthumously made Trustworthy Martial General and his son Shiji was summoned as an attendant in the Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved; Yuanyi was posthumously made Trustworthy Martial General and his son Shiji was appointed an attendant in the Ceremonial Service.

sentences.zh: 世勣後登進士第，奏名之日，上謂宰臣曰：「此神思子耶。」

translations.literal: Shiji later passed the jinshi examination; on the day names were announced the emperor said to the chief ministers: "Is this Shensi's son?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiji later passed the jinshi examination; when his name was announced the emperor asked the chief ministers, "Is this Shensi's son?"

sentences.zh: 歎賞者久之。

translations.literal: He sighed in admiration for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed in admiration for a long time.

sentences.zh: 元毅性沈厚，武勇過人，每讀書見古人忠義事，未嘗不嗟歎賞慕，喜動顏色，故臨難能死所事雲。

translations.literal: Yuanyi's nature was deep and steady and his martial valor surpassed others; whenever in reading he encountered ancient men's loyal and righteous deeds, he never failed to sigh, admire, and envy them, his face showing pleasure—thus in peril he could die for what he served.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi was grave and steady, surpassingly brave; reading of ancient loyalty and righteousness always moved him to sighs and brightened his face—so when crisis came he could die for his duty.

sentences.zh: 伯德梅和尚

translations.literal: Bode Meiheshang
translations.idiomatic: Bodemeiheshang

sentences.zh: 伯德梅和尚，泰州人也。

translations.literal: Bode Meiheshang was a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bodemeiheshang was from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 性鯁直，尚氣節。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and unyielding; he valued integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and unyielding and prized honor.

sentences.zh: 正隆五年，收充護衛，授曷魯碗群牧副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenglong he was enrolled as a guardsman and made Vice Superintendent of the Heluwan Herd Pastures.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 5 he joined the guards and was made vice superintendent of the Heluwan pastures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複召為護衛十人長，改尚廄局副使，遷本局使，轉右衛將軍拱衛使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned as Ten-Man Guards Captain, changed to Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Stables Office, promoted to Commissioner of that office, and transferred to Right Guard General and Palace Guard Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as ten-man guards captain, made vice commissioner then commissioner of the Imperial Stables, and promoted to right guard general and palace guard commissioner.

sentences.zh: 典尚廄者十餘年，積勞特遷官二階，除複州刺史。

translations.literal: He managed the Imperial Stables for more than ten years; for accumulated merit he was specially advanced two ranks and made Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years overseeing the imperial stables, he was specially promoted two ranks and made prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，為西北路副招討，收泰州防禦使，升武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: In early Mingchang he was Northwest Route Vice Pacification Commissioner, then Taizhou Defense Commissioner, and was promoted to Military Commissioner of Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Mingchang he was vice pacification commissioner on the Northwest Route, then defense commissioner of Taizhou, and was promoted to military commissioner of Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 六年，移鎮崇義軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to command Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was transferred to command Chongyi Army.

sentences.zh: 時有事北邊，左丞相夾谷清臣行省於臨潢，檄為副統。

translations.literal: When there was trouble on the northern border, Left Chancellor Jiagu Qingchen held provincial authority at Linhuang and summoned him as deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out on the northern frontier, left chancellor Jiagu Qingchen took provincial command at Linhuang and appointed him deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 會敵入臨潢，梅和尚暨護衛辟合土等領軍逆擊之。

translations.literal: When the enemy entered Linhuang, Meiheshang together with guardsman Bihetu and others led troops to strike them in counterattack.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy entered Linhuang, Meiheshang and the guardsman Bihetu led a counterattack.

sentences.zh: 敵積陣以待，梅和尚直搗其陣，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The enemy massed formations to await them; Meiheshang drove straight into their array and killed and wounded very many.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy formed deep ranks to receive them; Meiheshang charged straight in and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 敵知孤軍無繼，聚兵圍之。

translations.literal: The enemy knew the isolated force had no reinforcements and gathered troops to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they were isolated without reinforcements, the enemy massed and surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 度不能免，乃下馬相背射，複殺百餘人，矢盡猶以弓提擊，為流矢所中死，辟合土等皆沒。

translations.literal: Seeing escape was impossible, they dismounted and shot back to back, killing more than a hundred again; when arrows were spent they still struck with bow stocks, and Meiheshang died from a stray arrow; Bihetu and the others all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, they dismounted and fought back to back, killing another hundred; when their arrows ran out they clubbed with their bows until Meiheshang fell to a stray shaft; Bihetu and the rest perished with him.

sentences.zh: 上聞之震悼，詔贈龍虎衛上將軍，躐遷十階，特賜錢二十萬，命以禮葬之，特皆官給，以其子都奴為軍前猛安，中奴護喪，就差權同知臨潢府事李達可為敕祭使，同知德昌軍節度使事石抹和尚為敕葬使。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was deeply shocked and mourned; an edict posthumously made him Tiger-Dragon Guard General, skipped ten ranks in promotion, specially granted two hundred thousand cash, ordered burial with full rites—all expenses supplied by the state—made his son Dounu a front-line military colony chief, Zhongnu to escort the funeral, and appointed Acting Vice Commissioner of Linhuang Li Dake as imperial sacrifice commissioner and Vice Commissioner of Dechang Military Commission Shimo Heshang as imperial burial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply grieved, the emperor posthumously made him Tiger-Dragon Guard general, skipped ten ranks, granted two hundred thousand cash, and ordered a state funeral; his son Dounu was made a front-line colony chief, Zhongnu escorted the bier, Li Dake of Linhuang was named sacrifice commissioner, and Shimo Heshang of Dechang burial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，上諭尚書省曰：「梅和尚死王事，其子都奴從軍久有功，其議所以酬之。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an the emperor instructed the Secretariat: "Meiheshang died in the king's service; his son Dounu has long followed the army with merit—deliberate how to reward him."
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 5 the emperor told the Secretariat, "Meiheshang died for the state; his son Dounu has served long with merit—decide how to reward him."

sentences.zh: 乃命為典署丞。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Director of the Palace Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the palace records office.

sentences.zh: 烏古孫兀屯

translations.literal: Wugusun Wutun
translations.idiomatic: Wugusunwutun

sentences.zh: 烏古孫兀屯，上京路人。

translations.literal: Wugusun Wutun was a man of Shangjing Route.
translations.idiomatic: Wugusunwutun was from the Shangjing circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定末，襲猛安。

translations.literal: At the end of Dading he inherited a military colony.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dading he inherited a military colony.

sentences.zh: 明昌七年，以本兵充萬戶，備邊有功，除歸德軍節度副使，改盤安軍，察廉，遷同知速頻路節度使事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Mingchang, with his own troops he filled the post of Ten-Thousand Household Commander, had merit in border defense, was made Vice Commissioner of Guide Military Commission, changed to Pan'an Army, passed integrity inspection, and was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Supin Route Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 7 he led his own troops as ten-thousand-household commander, distinguished himself on the frontier, became vice commissioner of Guide, then Pan'an, passed an integrity review, and was made vice commissioner on the Supin circuit.

sentences.zh: 以憂去官，起複歸德府治中，遷唐州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of mourning he left office; recalled from mourning to serve as administrative aide of Guide Prefecture; transferred to Prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning, was recalled to serve as administrative aide of Guide Prefecture, and was then appointed Prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年四月，宋皇甫斌步騎萬人侵唐州，兀屯兵甚少，遣泌陽尉白散不、巡檢蒲閑各以五十人乘城拒守。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Taihe, the Song general Huangfu Bin invaded Tangzhou with ten thousand infantry and cavalry. Wutu had very few troops and sent the Miyang magistrate Bai Sanbu and the inspector Pu Xian, each with fifty men, to mount the walls and hold them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Taihe 6, the Song commander Huangfu Bin marched on Tangzhou with ten thousand foot and horse. Wutu's force was tiny; he sent the Miyang magistrate Bai Sanbu and the inspector Pu Xian, each with fifty men, to man the walls and resist.

sentences.zh: 兀屯見宋兵在城東北者可破，令軍事判官撒虎帶以精兵百人自西門出，繞出東北宋兵營後掩擊之，殺數十百人，宋兵大亂，迨夜乃遁去。

translations.literal: Wutu saw that the Song troops in the northeast of the city could be broken. He ordered the military aide Sagudai to take a hundred picked soldiers out through the west gate, circle behind the Song camp to the northeast, and strike from concealment, killing several tens to a hundred men. The Song army fell into great disorder and did not flee until night.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Song force northeast of the city could be broken, Wutu ordered his military aide Sagudai to lead a hundred elite troops out the west gate, swing around behind the Song camp to the northeast, and fall upon them. Dozens upon dozens were killed; the Song ranks collapsed in chaos and only fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 五月，皇甫斌複以兵數萬來攻，行省遣泌陽副巡檢納合軍勝救唐州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Huangfu Bin again came to attack with tens of thousands of troops. The Branch Secretariat sent the Miyang deputy inspector Nahe Junsheng to relieve Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Huangfu Bin returned with an army tens of thousands strong. The Branch Secretariat dispatched the Miyang deputy inspector Nahe Junsheng to rescue Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 兀屯出兵與軍勝合兵城東北，設伏兵以待之。

translations.literal: Wutu sent troops out and joined Junsheng northeast of the city, setting ambush troops to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Wutu marched out and united with Junsheng northeast of the city, laying ambushes to receive the enemy.

sentences.zh: 乃分騎兵為三，一出一入以致宋兵。

translations.literal: Then he divided the cavalry into three groups, one going out and one coming in to lure the Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his cavalry into three bands, sending them out and in by turns to draw the Song army on.

sentences.zh: 宋兵陷於淖，伏兵發，中沖宋兵為二，遂大潰。

translations.literal: The Song troops sank into the mire; the ambush troops sprang up, charging through the middle and cutting the Song army in two, whereupon it broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Song soldiers mired in the bog; the hidden troops rose at once, drove through their center and split the army in two, and a total rout followed.

sentences.zh: 追奔至湖陽，斬首萬餘級，獲馬三百匹。

translations.literal: They pursued the fleeing enemy to Huyang, beheading more than ten thousand and capturing three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran to Huyang, where more than ten thousand heads were taken and three hundred horses captured.

sentences.zh: 宋別將以兵三千來襲，遇之竹林寺，殪之。

translations.literal: A separate Song general came to raid with three thousand troops; they encountered him at Zhulin Temple and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: A Song deputy commander struck with three thousand men; they met him at Zhulin Temple and wiped his force out.

sentences.zh: 納合軍勝手殺宋將，取其金帶印章以獻。

translations.literal: Nahe Junsheng personally killed the Song general, took his gold belt and seal, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Nahe Junsheng slew the Song commander with his own hand, seized his gold belt and seal, and presented them as trophies.

sentences.zh: 詔遷兀屯同知河南府事，軍勝遷梁縣令，各進兩階。

translations.literal: An edict transferred Wutu to Deputy Commissioner of Henan Prefecture and Junsheng to Magistrate of Liang County; each was promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Wutu was made Deputy Commissioner of Henan Prefecture and Junsheng Magistrate of Liang County; both were advanced two ranks.

sentences.zh: 兀屯賞銀三百五十兩、重彩十端，為右副元帥完顏匡右翼都統。

translations.literal: Wutu was rewarded with three hundred fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy brocade, and served as Right Wing Commander under the Right Deputy Marshal Wanyan Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wutu received three hundred fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of fine brocade, and served as Right Wing Commander on the staff of the Right Deputy Marshal Wanyan Kuang.

sentences.zh: 匡取棗陽，遣元屯襲神馬坡，宋兵五萬人夾水陣，以強弩拒岸，兀屯分兵奪其三橋，自辰至午連拔十三柵，遂取神馬坡。

translations.literal: Kuang took Zaoyang and sent Wutu to strike Shenmapo. Fifty thousand Song troops drew up their formation across the water and used powerful crossbows to hold the bank. Wutu divided his force and seized their three bridges; from the hour of chen to the hour of wu he took thirteen stockades in succession and thus captured Shenmapo.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuang captured Zaoyang he sent Wutu against Shenmapo. Fifty thousand Song soldiers formed their line across the water, strong crossbows bristling along the shore. Wutu divided his men, seized all three bridges, and from morning through midday stormed thirteen stockades in a row until Shenmapo fell.

sentences.zh: 從攻襄，至漢江，兀屯亂流徑度。

translations.literal: He joined the attack on Xiangyang; when they reached the Han River, Wutu crossed directly through the turbulent current.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the assault on Xiangyang, and when the army reached the Han River Wutu plunged straight across the racing current.

sentences.zh: 複進一階，號平南虎威將軍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted one rank and given the title General Who Pacifies the South with Tiger Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted one rank further and ennobled as General Who Pacifies the South with Tiger Might.

sentences.zh: 宋人請和，遷河南副統軍。

translations.literal: When the Song sought peace, he was transferred to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song sued for peace he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan.

sentences.zh: 大安初，遷昌武軍節度使，副統軍如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Changwu Army, while retaining his post as Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Da'an era he became Military Commissioner of the Changwu Army, keeping his rank as Deputy Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷西南路招討使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 兀屯禦下嚴酷，軍士多亡，杖六十。

translations.literal: Wutu was harsh toward those under him; many soldiers fled, and he was punished with sixty strokes of the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Wutu ruled his men with brutal severity; so many soldiers deserted that he was sentenced to sixty strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 除同知上京留守事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Shangjing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Shangjing Garrison.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，將兵二萬入衛中都，遷元帥右都監、轉左都監，兼北京留守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he led twenty thousand troops to defend the Central Capital, was promoted to Right Director of the Marshalate, then transferred to Left Director, and concurrently served as Garrison Commissioner of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an 3 he marched twenty thousand men to the defense of the Central Capital, rose to Right Director of the Marshalate, then to Left Director, and at the same time held the post of Garrison Commissioner of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 有功，賜金吐鶻、重彩十端。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted a golden touhu ornament and ten bolts of heavy brocade.
translations.idiomatic: For distinguished service he received a golden touhu ornament and ten bolts of fine brocade.

sentences.zh: 遷元帥左監軍，留守如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Overseer of the Marshalate, retaining his garrison commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Overseer of the Marshalate while continuing as garrison commissioner.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年閏月，以兵入衛中都，詔以兵萬六千人守定興，軍敗，兀屯戰沒。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the first year of Zhenyou he led troops to defend the Central Capital; by edict he was ordered with sixteen thousand men to hold Dingxing. The army was defeated and Wutu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of Zhenyou 1 he marched to the defense of the Central Capital and was ordered to hold Dingxing with sixteen thousand men. The army was broken and Wutu fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 高守約

translations.literal: Gao Shouyue
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shouyue

sentences.zh: 高守約，字從簡，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Gao Shouyue, courtesy name Congjian, was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shouyue, styled Congjian, came from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年進士，累官觀州刺史。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-eighth year of Dading, he rose through successive offices to Prefect of Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Dading 28 and rose through successive posts until he became Prefect of Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 大元兵徇地河朔，郭邦獻已歸順，從至城下，呼守約曰：「從簡當計全家室。」

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army overran the lands of Hebei, Guo Bangxian had already surrendered and followed them to the foot of the wall, calling to Shouyue: "Congjian ought to think of saving your whole household."
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of the Great Yuan swept through Hebei, Guo Bangxian, who had already gone over to them, came with the besiegers to the foot of the wall and shouted to Shouyue, "Congjian—think of your family's lives."

sentences.zh: 守約弗顧，至再三，寧約厲聲曰：「吾不汝識也。」

translations.literal: Shouyue paid no heed; when this was repeated again and again, Shouyue said in a stern voice: "I do not know you."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue ignored him. When the appeal was pressed again and again, he answered in a harsh voice, "I do not know you."

sentences.zh: 城破被執，使之跪，守約不屈，遂死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was captured; they made him kneel, but Shouyue would not submit and so died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was taken prisoner. They forced him to his knees, but Shouyue would not yield, and so he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔贈崇義軍節度使，諡忠敬。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously granted the post of Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army and given the posthumous title Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army and honored him with the posthumous name Zhongjing, "Loyal and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 和速嘉安禮

translations.literal: Hesujia Anli
translations.idiomatic: Hesujia Anli

sentences.zh: 和速嘉安禮，字子敬，本名酌，大名路人。

translations.literal: Hesujia Anli, courtesy name Zijing, original name Zhuo, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Hesujia Anli, styled Zijing, whose original name was Zhuo, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 穎悟博學，淹貫經史。

translations.literal: Keen and quick-witted, broadly learned, he was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Quick of mind and wide in learning, he had mastered the full span of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-eighth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Dading 28.

sentences.zh: 至寧末，為泰安州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhiqing era he was Prefect of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhiqing reign he served as Prefect of Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，山東被兵，郡縣望風而遁，或勸安禮去之，安禮曰：「我去，城誰與守，且避難負國家之恩乎？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, Shandong was ravaged by war; prefectures and counties fled at the first rumor. Some urged Anli to leave, but Anli said: "If I leave, who will hold the city? And would fleeing to save myself not betray the grace the state has shown me?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyou opened, war swept Shandong; prefectures and counties broke and ran at the mere rumor of the enemy. Some urged Anli to withdraw, but he said, "If I go, who will guard this city? And how could I flee for safety without betraying the debt I owe the state?"

sentences.zh: 乃團練繕完，為禦守計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he organized militia training and repairs and made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then drilled the militia, repaired the defenses, and prepared the city to stand a siege.

sentences.zh: 已而大元兵至，戰旬日不能下，謂之曰：「此孤城耳，內無糧儲，外無兵援，不降無遺類矣。」

translations.literal: Before long the Great Yuan army arrived; they fought for ten days and could not take the city. They said to him: "This is but an isolated city—no grain stored within, no relief from without. If you do not surrender, not one soul will be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Great Yuan forces arrived. Ten days of fighting failed to bring the walls down, and they told him, "This is a lone city—no stores within, no help without. Surrender, or not one life will remain."
