sentences.zh: 安禮不聽。

translations.literal: Anli would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Anli refused to heed them.

sentences.zh: 城破被執，初不識其為誰，或妄以酒監對，安禮曰：「我刺史也，何以諱為？」

translations.literal: When the city fell he was captured. At first they did not know who he was; some falsely claimed to be the wine inspector. Anli said: "I am the prefect—why should I conceal my identity?"
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was taken. At first his captors did not know who he was; some tried to pass themselves off as the wine inspector. Anli said, "I am the prefect—why should I hide who I am?"

sentences.zh: 使之跪，安禮不屈，遂以戈撞其胸而殺之。

translations.literal: They made him kneel, but Anli would not submit; they then struck his chest with a halberd and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered him to kneel, but Anli would not bow. They ran a halberd through his chest and killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈泰定軍節度使，諡堅貞。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously granted the post of Military Commissioner of the Taiding Army and given the posthumous title Jianzhen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Military Commissioner of the Taiding Army and gave him the posthumous name Jianzhen, "Steadfast and Upright."

sentences.zh: 王維翰

translations.literal: Wang Weihan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weihan

sentences.zh: 王維翰，字之翰，利州龍山人。

translations.literal: Wang Weihan, courtesy name Zhihan, was a native of Longshan in Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weihan, styled Zhihan, came from Longshan in Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 父庭，遼季率縣人保縣東山，後以眾降。

translations.literal: His father Ting, at the end of the Liao, led the people of the county to hold Dongshan in the county; later he surrendered with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ting, in the closing years of the Liao, rallied the county and held Dongshan; he later submitted with his men.

sentences.zh: 維翰好學不倦，中大定二十八年進士。

translations.literal: Weihan loved learning and never wearied of it; he passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan was an indefatigable scholar and passed the jinshi examination in Dading 28.

sentences.zh: 調貴德州軍事判官，察廉遷永霸令。

translations.literal: He was assigned as military aide of Guide Prefecture; through an integrity inspection he was promoted to Magistrate of Yongba.
translations.idiomatic: He began as military aide of Guide Prefecture and, after a merit review for integrity, was promoted to magistrate of Yongba.

sentences.zh: 縣豪欲嘗試維翰，設事陳訴，維翰窮竟之，遂伏其詐，杖殺之，健訟衰息。

translations.literal: A local magnate in the county wished to test Weihan; he set up a case and filed a petition. Weihan investigated it to the end, whereupon the man confessed to fraud and was beaten to death; aggressive litigation then died away.
translations.idiomatic: A county strongman sought to test Weihan's mettle and manufactured a lawsuit. Weihan pursued the matter to its root, exposed the fraud, and had the man beaten to death; thereafter the fever of vexatious litigation cooled.

sentences.zh: 曆弘政、獲嘉令，佐胥持國治河決，有勞，遷一階。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Hongzheng and Huojia, assisted Xu Chiguo in treating a river breach, and for his labor was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Hongzheng and Huojia in turn, aided Xu Chiguo in repairing a river breach, and was promoted one rank for his efforts.

sentences.zh: 改北京轉運戶籍判官，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He was changed to household-registration aide of the Beijing Transport Commission and was appointed a clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became household-registration aide on the Beijing Transport Commission and was then appointed a clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 除同知保靜軍節度使事，檢括戶籍，一郡稱平。

translations.literal: He was appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of the Baojing Army; he audited household registers, and the whole commandery was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: As Deputy Military Commissioner of the Baojing Army he audited the household registers, and the entire commandery came to be known as fairly governed.

sentences.zh: 屬縣有奴殺其主人者，誣主人弟殺之，刑部疑之。

translations.literal: In a subordinate county a slave killed his master and falsely accused the master's younger brother of the killing; the Ministry of Justice was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: In one subordinate county a slave murdered his master and tried to frame the master's younger brother for the deed; the Ministry of Justice found the case doubtful.

sentences.zh: 維翰審讞，乃微行物色之，得其狀，奴遂引服。

translations.literal: Weihan tried the case, then went in disguise to investigate and obtained the facts; the slave then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan heard the case, then went about in plain dress to gather evidence; once the truth was found, the slave confessed.

sentences.zh: 改中都轉運副使，攝侍御史，奏事殿中，章宗曰：「佳禦史。」

translations.literal: He was changed to Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital and acted as Censor; when he memorialized in the hall, Emperor Zhangzong said: "An excellent censor."
translations.idiomatic: He became Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital and served as acting Censor. When he presented a memorial in court, Emperor Zhangzong remarked, "A fine censor."

sentences.zh: 就除侍御史。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon confirmed as Censor.

sentences.zh: 改左司員外郎，轉右司朗中。

translations.literal: He was changed to Assistant Director of the Left Department and transferred to Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Assistant Director of the Left Department and then Director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 僕散揆伐宋，維翰行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: When Pusan Kui campaigned against the Song, Weihan served as Director of the Left and Right Departments on the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Pusan Kui's campaign against Song, Weihan served on the Branch Secretariat as Director of the Left and Right Departments.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，河南旱蝗，詔維翰體究田禾分數以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe Henan suffered drought and locusts; an edict ordered Weihan to investigate thoroughly the condition of the fields and crops by proportion and report.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 7 drought and locusts struck Henan; the throne ordered Weihan to survey field and crop losses in detail and report back.

sentences.zh: 七月，雨，複詔維翰曰：「雨雖沾足，秋種過時，使多種蔬菜猶愈於荒萊也。

translations.literal: In the seventh month it rained, and another edict to Weihan said: "Though the rain has soaked the ground sufficiently, the season for autumn planting has passed; having people plant more vegetables is still better than leaving the land waste.
translations.idiomatic: When rain came in the seventh month, a further edict told Weihan, "Though the rains have finally soaked the earth, the season for autumn grain is already gone—better to have the people sow vegetables widely than leave the fields to lie fallow.

sentences.zh: 蝗蝻遺子，如何可絕？」

translations.literal: Locust nymphs leave offspring—how can they be exterminated entirely?"
translations.idiomatic: Locust nymphs leave broods behind—how can they be wiped out altogether?"

sentences.zh: 舊有蝗處來歲宜菽麥，諭百姓使知之。」

translations.literal: In places where locusts appeared before, beans and wheat should be planted next year; instruct the common people and make them know this.
translations.idiomatic: Where locusts have been, beans and wheat should be sown the following year—make this known to the people."

sentences.zh: 八年，宋人受盟，還為右司郎中，進官一階。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Song accepted the treaty, he returned to his post as Director of the Right Department and was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the Song accepted the peace treaty, he resumed his post as Director of the Right Department and was advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 上問：「宋人請和複能背盟否？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "The Song sought peace—can they again break the treaty?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "The Song have sued for peace—might they break the treaty again?"

sentences.zh: 維翰對曰：「宋主怠于政事，南兵佻弱，兩淮兵後千里蕭條，其臣懲韓侂胄、蘇師旦，無複敢執其咎者，不足憂也。

translations.literal: Weihan replied: "The Song ruler is negligent in government; southern troops are frivolous and weak; after the warfare in the Two Huai a thousand li lie desolate; his ministers, chastened by Han Tuozhou and Su Shidan, no longer dare take such blame upon themselves. They are not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan answered, "The Song emperor neglects his duties; southern armies are light and weak; a thousand li of the Two Huai country lies wasted after the war; and his courtiers, still smarting from Han Tuozhou and Su Shidan, will not again dare court such disaster. They are no cause for concern.

sentences.zh: 唯北方當勞聖慮耳。」

translations.literal: Only the north should occupy Your Majesty's concern."
translations.idiomatic: It is the north alone that should weigh upon Your Majesty's mind."

sentences.zh: 久之，遷大理卿、兼潞王傅，同知審官院事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Chief Justice, concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Lu, and Deputy Director of the Office of Personnel Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In time he rose to Chief Justice, became Tutor to the Prince of Lu, and served as Deputy Director of the Office of Personnel Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 新格，教坊樂工階至四品，換文武正資，服金紫。

translations.literal: Under new regulations, musicians of the Entertainment Bureau whose rank reached the fourth grade exchanged for regular civil and military ranks and wore gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: New regulations allowed Entertainment Bureau musicians who reached the fourth rank to exchange into regular civil and military grades and wear gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 維翰奏：「伶優賤工，衣縉紳之服，非所以尊朝廷也。」

translations.literal: Weihan memorialized: "Actors and low craftsmen wearing the robes of officials—this is not the way to honor the court."
translations.idiomatic: Weihan submitted a memorial: "For actors and base artisans to dress as court officials is no way to uphold the dignity of the throne."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 大安初，權右諫議大夫，三司欲稅間架，維翰諫不聽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an, as Acting Right Remonstrance Grandee, when the Three Departments wished to levy a building-frame tax, Weihan remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Da'an era, while serving as Acting Right Remonstrance Grandee, he opposed the Three Departments' plan to impose a building-frame tax; his remonstrance went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 轉禦史中丞，無何，遷工部尚書、兼大理卿，改刑部尚書，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; before long he was promoted to Minister of Works and concurrently Chief Justice, then changed to Minister of Justice, and appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Censor-in-Chief, and soon afterward Minister of Works and Chief Justice, then Minister of Justice, and finally Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，罷為定海軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was dismissed and made Military Commissioner of the Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhenyou he was removed from the council and appointed Military Commissioner of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，道路不通，維翰舟行遇盜，呼謂之曰：「爾輩本良民，因亂至此，財物不惜，勿恐吾家。」

translations.literal: At that time the roads were impassable; Weihan traveled by boat and encountered bandits. He called to them: "You were originally good people and came to this through chaos. I do not begrudge my goods—do not fear harm to my household."
translations.idiomatic: The roads were cut off, and traveling by boat Weihan fell in with bandits. He called out to them, "You were honest folk once, driven to this by disorder. Take what you will—I do not begrudge my goods, and do not fear that I will bring harm upon your families."

sentences.zh: 盜感其言而去。

translations.literal: Moved by his words, the bandits departed.
translations.idiomatic: Touched by his words, the bandits went away.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，無兵備，鄰郡皆望風奔潰，維翰謂吏民曰：「孤城不可守。

translations.literal: When he reached his post there was no military preparedness; neighboring prefectures all fled at the first rumor. Weihan told the officials and people: "An isolated city cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his command he found no forces to defend it; neighboring prefectures had already broken and run at rumor of the enemy. Weihan told officials and commoners alike, "This lone city cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 此州阻山浮海，當有生地，無俱為魚肉也。」

translations.literal: This prefecture is blocked by mountains and faces the sea; there must be a way to live. Let us not all become fish on the chopping block."
translations.idiomatic: Mountains hem this prefecture in on one side and the sea lies open on the other—there must be paths to safety. Let us not all be butchered together."

sentences.zh: 乃縱百姓避難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released the common people to flee for safety.
translations.idiomatic: He then allowed the people to disperse and seek refuge.

sentences.zh: 維翰率吏民願從者奔東北山，結營堡自守，力窮被執不肯降。

translations.literal: Weihan led the officials and people who wished to follow him to flee to the mountains in the northeast, established a fortified camp, and defended himself; when his strength was exhausted he was captured but would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan led those officials and people willing to follow him into the northeastern hills, built a fortified camp, and held out until, spent and captured, he still refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 妻姚氏亦不肯屈，與維翰俱死。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Yao, also would not submit and died together with Weihan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Yao, likewise refused to yield and died with him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈中奉大夫，姚氏芮國夫人，諡貞潔。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously granted the rank of Zhongfeng Daifu; Lady Yao was granted the title Lady of Ruiguo; he was given the posthumous title Zhenjie.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Zhongfeng Daifu, created Lady Yao Lady of Ruiguo, and honored him with the posthumous name Zhenjie, "Chaste and Pure."

sentences.zh: 移剌古與涅

translations.literal: Yila Guyunie
translations.idiomatic: Yilaguyunie

sentences.zh: 移剌古與涅，安化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Yila Guyunie, Military Commissioner of the Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yilaguyunie was Military Commissioner of the Anhua Army.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，大元年兵取密州，古與涅率兵力戰，流矢連中其頸，既拔去複中其頰，死焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, when the Great Yuan army took Mizhou, Guyunie led troops and fought fiercely; stray arrows struck his neck in succession, and after they were pulled out another struck his cheek, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhenyou, when the Great Yuan forces seized Mizhou, Guyunie led his men in fierce resistance. Stray arrows pierced his neck one after another; even after they were drawn out, another struck his cheek, and he fell dead.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，詔贈安遠大將軍、知益都府事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou an edict posthumously granted him the title General Who Pacifies the Distant and Knowledge of Yizhou Prefecture Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 3 an edict posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Yizhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋扆，中都宛平人也。

translations.literal: Song Yi was a native of Wanping in the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yi came from Wanping in the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 正隆五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifth year of Zhenglong.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Zhenglong 5.

sentences.zh: 曆辰州、寧化州軍事判官，曹王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He served successively as military aide of Chenzhou and Ninghuazhou and as secretary to the household of the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military aide of Chenzhou and Ninghuazhou and as secretary in the household of the Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 陝西西路轉運都勾判官。

translations.literal: Chief auditor of the Shaanxi West Circuit Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief auditor of the Shaanxi West Circuit Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史，除武定軍節度副使、中都右警巡使。

translations.literal: He was appointed a clerk in the Secretariat, then Deputy Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army and Right Patrol Inspector of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Secretariat as a clerk, then was made Deputy Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army and Right Patrol Inspector of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 時固安縣丞劉昭與部民裴原爭買鄰田，扆用昭屬，抑原使毋爭。

translations.literal: At the time the Gu'an county assistant Liu Zhao and a local resident named Pei Yuan competed to buy neighboring fields; Yi favored Zhao's faction and suppressed Yuan so that he would not compete.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gu'an county assistant Liu Zhao and a local man named Pei Yuan bid against each other for neighboring land, Yi sided with Zhao's party and forced Yuan to withdraw his claim.

sentences.zh: 禦史台劾奏，奪一官，解職，降廣寧府推官。

translations.literal: The Censorate impeached and memorialized; he was stripped of one rank, removed from office, and demoted to judicial officer of Guangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate impeached him; he lost one rank, was dismissed from office, and was demoted to judicial officer of Guangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改遼東路鹽使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Salt Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Salt Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複吏部員外郎，曆薊、曹、景州刺史，同知中都路轉運使事，遷北京、臨潢等路按察使。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he left office for mourning, was recalled from mourning as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, served successively as Prefect of Ji, Cao, and Jing, as Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit, and was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Beijing, Linhuang, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled to serve as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, held successive prefectures at Ji, Cao, and Jing, became Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit, and rose to Surveillance Commissioner over Beijing, Linhuang, and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 改安國軍節度使、河東南路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army and Transport Commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army and Transport Commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 禦史劾其前任按察侵民舍不稱職，降沂州防禦使，移浚州，遷山東西路轉運使，改定海軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Censorate impeached him for, during his earlier tenure as surveillance commissioner, encroaching on private dwellings and not fulfilling his duties; he was demoted to Defender of Yizhou, transferred to Xunzhou, promoted to Transport Commissioner of the Shandong East-West Circuit, and changed to Military Commissioner of the Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Censors charged that in his earlier surveillance post he had seized private homes and failed in his duties; he was reduced to Defender of Yizhou, moved to Xunzhou, later made Transport Commissioner of the Shandong East-West Circuit, and finally Military Commissioner of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，改沁南軍，正月，大元兵至懷州，城破死焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to the Qinnan Army; in the first month, when the Great Yuan army reached Huaizhou, the city fell and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 he was transferred to the Qinnan Army; in the first month, when the Great Yuan forces reached Huaizhou, the city fell and he perished there.

sentences.zh: 扆天資刻酷，所至不容物，以是蹭蹬於世雲。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature harsh and cruel; wherever he went he tolerated nothing, and for this reason it is said he stumbled in his career.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was harsh and unforgiving by nature and brooked no dissent wherever he served; it is said that for this his career never prospered.

sentences.zh: 烏古論榮祖

translations.literal: Wugulun Rongzu
translations.idiomatic: Wugulunrongzu

sentences.zh: 烏古論榮祖，本名福興，河間人。

translations.literal: Wugulun Rongzu, original name Fuxing, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulunrongzu, whose original name was Fuxing, came from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年進士，曆官補尚書省令史，除都轉運司都勾判官，轉弘文校理，升中都總管府判官，察廉除震武軍節度副使、彰德府司馬，累遷戶部員外郎、甯海州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he passed the jinshi examination; he served in successive posts as a supplemental clerk in the Secretariat, was appointed chief auditor of the Transport Commission, transferred to collator in the Hongwen Academy, promoted to judge of the Central Capital Chief Administrator's office, and after an integrity inspection was made Deputy Military Commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and Administrator of Zhangde Prefecture; he rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Prefect of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Mingchang 2 and rose through a succession of posts: supplemental Secretariat clerk, chief auditor of the Transport Commission, Hongwen Academy collator, and judge of the Central Capital Chief Administrator's office. After an integrity inspection he was appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and Administrator of Zhangde Prefecture, and eventually became Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Prefect of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年城破，榮祖猶力戰，死之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou the city fell; Rongzu still fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2, when the city fell, Rongzu fought on to the last and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈安武軍節度使，賜諡毅勇。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army and bestowed the posthumous title Yiyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army and honored with the posthumous name Yiyong, "Resolute and Brave."

sentences.zh: 烏古論仲溫

translations.literal: Wugulun Zhongwen
translations.idiomatic: Wugulunzhongwen

sentences.zh: 烏古論仲溫，本名胡剌，蓋州按春猛安人。

translations.literal: Wugulun Zhongwen, original name Hula, was a native of the Anchun military colony in Gaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulunzhongwen, whose original name was Hula, came from the Anchun military colony in Gaizhou.

sentences.zh: 大定二十五年進士，累官太學助教、應奉翰林文字、河東路提刑判官，改河北東路轉運副使。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-fifth year of Dading; he served successively as assistant instructor of the Grand Academy, Hanlin drafting official, and judicial aide of the Hedong Circuit, and was changed to Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Hebei East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Dading 25 and served in turn as Grand Academy assistant instructor, Hanlin drafting official, and judicial aide on the Hedong Circuit before becoming Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Hebei East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 禦史薦前任提刑稱職，遷同知順天軍節度使事，簽上京、東京等路按察司事，改提舉肇州漕運、兼同知武興軍節度使事、東勝州刺史。

translations.literal: The Censorate recommended his performance as former judicial commissioner; he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Shuntian Army, registrar of the Shangjing and Tokyo circuit surveillance commissions, and changed to Commissioner of Zhaozhou grain transport, concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Wuxing Army and Prefect of Dongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Censors commended his record as a former judicial commissioner, and he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Shuntian Army and registrar for the Shangjing and Tokyo circuit surveillance commissions. He was then made Commissioner of Zhaozhou grain transport, concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Wuxing Army and Prefect of Dongsheng.

sentences.zh: 坐前在上京不稱職，降鎮寧軍節度副使。

translations.literal: For earlier failure in office at Shangjing, he was demoted to Deputy Military Commissioner of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had performed poorly at Shangjing, he was reduced to Deputy Military Commissioner of the Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 改滑州刺史、河東南路按察副使、壽州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of Huazhou, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit, and Defender of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Prefect of Huazhou, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit, and Defender of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，遷鎮西軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhenxi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhenyou he was made Military Commissioner of the Zhenxi Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，中都被圍，遂至太原，移書安撫使賈益謙，約以鄉兵救中都。

translations.literal: At that time the Central Capital was besieged; he went to Taiyuan and wrote to Pacification Commissioner Jia Yiqian, agreeing to raise local militia to relieve the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital was then under siege. Zhongwen went to Taiyuan and wrote to Pacification Commissioner Jia Yiqian, proposing to raise local militia for its relief.

sentences.zh: 因馳驛如平陽，將與益謙會於絳，不能進，抵平陽而還。

translations.literal: He rode post-haste to Pingyang, intending to meet Yiqian at Jiang, but could not advance; he reached Pingyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped by post relay to Pingyang, intending to join Yiqian at Jiang, but could not get through. He reached Pingyang and turned back.

sentences.zh: 仲溫嘗治平陽，吏民爭留之，仲溫曰：「平陽巨鎮，易為守禦，于私計得矣，如嵐州何。」

translations.literal: Zhongwen had once governed Pingyang; officials and people vied to keep him. Zhongwen said: "Pingyang is a great fortress, easy to defend—for my private interests that would do well enough, but what of Lanzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen had once governed Pingyang, and officials and commoners alike begged him to stay. He said, "Pingyang is a great stronghold, easy to hold—for my own sake that would be well enough. But what of Lanzhou?"

sentences.zh: 遂還鎮。

translations.literal: And so he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: And so he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 已而大元兵大至，城破，不屈而死。

translations.literal: Before long the Great Yuan army arrived in force; the city fell, and he died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Great Yuan forces arrived in overwhelming strength. The city fell, and he died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 贈資德大夫、婆速路兵馬都總管，諡忠毅，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Zide Dafu and Overall Commander of Basu Circuit forces, given the posthumous title Zhongyi, and seasonal sacrifices were offered.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Zide Dafu and Overall Commander of Basu Circuit forces, honored with the posthumous name Zhongyi, "Loyal and Resolute," and granted seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 九住，宗室子，為武州刺史，唐括孛果速為軍事判官。

translations.literal: Jiu Zhu, an imperial clansman, was Prefect of Wuzhou; Tangguo Boguosu was military aide.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Zhu, a member of the imperial clan, served as Prefect of Wuzhou, with Tangguo Boguosu as his military aide.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年十一月，大元兵取九住子侄抵城下，謂之曰：「山東、河北今皆降我，汝之家屬我亦得已，苟不速降，且殺之也。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Zhenyou, the Great Yuan army brought Jiu Zhu's sons and nephews to the foot of the wall and said to him: "Shandong and Hebei have all surrendered to us now; we have also captured your family. If you do not surrender promptly, we shall kill them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhenyou 2, the Great Yuan army brought Jiu Zhu's sons and nephews to the foot of the wall and called out to him: "Shandong and Hebei have all surrendered to us, and we hold your family as well. Surrender at once, or we will kill them."

sentences.zh: 九住曰：「當以死報國，遑恤家為。」

translations.literal: Jiu Zhu said: "One should repay the state with death—how could I spare a thought for my family?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Zhu replied, "A man should repay his state with his life. What room is there to worry about his household?"

sentences.zh: 無何，城破，力戰而死，孛果速亦不屈死焉。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; he fought fiercely and died, and Boguosu likewise died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell. Jiu Zhu fought to the death, and Boguosu likewise refused to yield and was killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈九住臨海軍節度使，加驃騎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: By edict Jiu Zhu was posthumously granted Military Commissioner of the Linhai Army and promoted to Upper General of the Flying Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Jiu Zhu as Military Commissioner of the Linhai Army and promoted him to Upper General of the Flying Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 孛果速建州刺史，加鎮國上將軍。

translations.literal: Boguosu was made Prefect of Jianzhou and promoted to Zhenguo Upper General.
translations.idiomatic: Boguosu was posthumously made Prefect of Jianzhou and promoted to Zhenguo Upper General.

sentences.zh: 仍令樹碑，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: They were also ordered memorial steles erected, with seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial steles were also ordered for them, with sacrifices at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 李演，字巨川，任城人。

translations.literal: Li Yan, courtesy name Juchuan, was a native of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, styled Juchuan, came from Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年進士第一，除應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: Top jinshi of the sixth year of Taihe; he was appointed Hanlin drafting official.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the jinshi examination of Taihe 6 and was appointed Hanlin drafting official.

sentences.zh: 再丁父母憂，居鄉里，貞祐初，任城被兵，演墨衰為濟州刺史，畫守禦策。

translations.literal: Twice he mourned his parents and lived in his home district. Early in Zhenyou, when Rencheng came under attack, Yan put on unhemmed mourning dress and acted as Prefect of Jizhou, drawing up defensive plans.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he left office to mourn his parents and returned to his home district. Early in Zhenyou, when Rencheng came under attack, Yan donned unhemmed mourning garb, assumed the duties of Prefect of Jizhou, and laid out a plan of defense.

sentences.zh: 召集州人為兵。

translations.literal: He summoned the people of the prefecture to serve as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He called up the people of the prefecture as troops.

sentences.zh: 搏戰三日，眾皆市人不能戰，逃散。

translations.literal: After three days of fierce fighting, the men were all townspeople who could not fight and fled in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: They fought hard for three days, but the force was made up of townspeople who could not hold the line, and they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 演被執，大將見其冠服非常，且知其名，問之曰：「汝非李應奉乎？」

translations.literal: Yan was captured; the general saw his unusual cap and robes and knew his name, and asked: "Are you not Li the Hanlin Drafting Official?
translations.idiomatic: Yan was taken prisoner. The enemy general, struck by his unusual cap and robes and already knowing his name, asked, "Are you not Li the Hanlin drafting official?"

sentences.zh: 演答曰：「我是也。」

translations.literal: Yan answered: "I am."
translations.idiomatic: Yan answered, "I am."

sentences.zh: 使之跪，不肯，以好語撫之，亦不聽，許之官祿，演曰：「我書生也，本朝何負於我，而利人之官祿哉！」

translations.literal: They made him kneel, but he refused; they tried to soothe him with kind words, but he would not listen; they promised him offices and salary, and Yan said: "I am a scholar—what has our dynasty done to wrong me, that I should covet another's rank and salary!"
translations.idiomatic: They ordered him to kneel, but he refused. They tried to win him with gentle words; he would not heed them. They offered him office and emolument. Yan said, "I am a scholar. What has this dynasty ever done to wrong me, that I should crave another man's rank and pay?"

sentences.zh: 大將怒，擊折其脛，遂曳出殺之，時年三十餘。

translations.literal: The general in anger struck and broke his shins, then dragged him out and killed him. He was a little over thirty.
translations.idiomatic: The general in a rage struck and broke his shins, then had him dragged out and killed. He was a little over thirty.

sentences.zh: 贈濟州刺史，詔有司為立碑雲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Prefect of Jizhou; an edict ordered the authorities to erect a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prefect of Jizhou, and the court ordered the authorities to raise a memorial stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 劉德基

translations.literal: Liu Deji
translations.idiomatic: Liu Deji

sentences.zh: 劉德基，大興人。

translations.literal: Liu Deji was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Deji came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年，特賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyou he was specially granted jinshi standing.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 1 he was specially granted jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 守官邊邑，夏兵攻城，德基坐査事，積薪其傍，謂家人曰「城破即焚我。」

translations.literal: Holding office in a border town, when Xia troops attacked the city Deji was conducting an investigation; he piled firewood beside him and told his family: "If the city falls, burn me at once."
translations.idiomatic: While serving in a border town, he was conducting an investigation when Xia troops besieged the city. He piled firewood beside him and told his family, "If the city falls, burn me at once."

sentences.zh: 及城破，其家人不忍縱火，遂被執。

translations.literal: When the city did fall, his family could not bear to set the fire, and so he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, his family could not bring themselves to light the fire, and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 脅使跪降，德基不屈。

translations.literal: They threatened him and made him kneel to surrender, but Deji would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: They forced him to his knees and demanded his surrender, but Deji would not yield.

sentences.zh: 同僚故人紿夏人曰：「此人素病狂，故敢如此。」

translations.literal: A colleague and old friend deceived the Xia troops, saying: "This man has long been deranged—that is why he dares act so.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague and old friend tried to deceive the Xia troops, saying, "This man has always been mad—that is why he dares behave this way."

sentences.zh: 德基曰：「為臣子當如此爾，吾豈狂耶？」

translations.literal: Deji said: "As a subject one ought to behave like this—how am I mad?
translations.idiomatic: Deji said, "This is how a subject ought to act. In what way am I mad?"

sentences.zh: 夏人壯其義，乃系諸獄，冀其改圖。

translations.literal: The Xia troops admired his integrity and imprisoned him, hoping he would change his mind.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia troops admired his steadfastness and threw him into prison, hoping he might yet change his mind.

sentences.zh: 已而召問，德基大罵，終不能從，曰：「吾豈苟生者哉！」

translations.literal: Later they summoned and questioned him; Deji cursed them fiercely and could never be made to yield, saying: "Am I one who clings to life!"
translations.idiomatic: Later they summoned him for questioning. Deji cursed them savagely and still would not submit, crying, "Do you think I am a man who clings to life!"

sentences.zh: 遂害之。

translations.literal: And so they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: And so they put him to death.

sentences.zh: 贈朝列大夫、同知通遠軍節度使事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Chaolie Dafu and Vice Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Chaolie Dafu and Vice Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 王毅，大興人。

translations.literal: Wang Yi was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 經義進士，累官東明令。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Classics examination; he rose through the posts to Magistrate of Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the Classics examination, he rose through successive posts to Magistrate of Dongming.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，東明圍急，毅率民兵願戰者數百人拒守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when the siege of Dongming grew desperate, Yi led several hundred militiamen who volunteered to fight and held the defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2, when the siege of Dongming grew desperate, Yi rallied several hundred militiamen who volunteered to fight and led them in the defense.

sentences.zh: 城破，毅猶率眾抗戰，力窮被執，與縣人王八等四人同驅之郭外。

translations.literal: When the city fell Yi still led the crowd in resistance; exhausted, he was captured and, together with four men of the county including Wang Ba, was driven outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Yi still led the people in resistance. At last, spent and captured, he was driven outside the wall together with four county men, including Wang Ba.

sentences.zh: 先殺二人，王八即前跪將降，毅以足踣之，厲聲曰：「忠臣不佐二主，汝乃降乎！」

translations.literal: Two were killed first; Wang Ba came forward and knelt to surrender, and Yi kicked him down and cried in a stern voice: "A loyal minister does not serve two masters—and you would surrender!
translations.idiomatic: Two were killed first. Wang Ba stepped forward and knelt to surrender. Yi kicked him to the ground and shouted, "A loyal minister does not serve two masters—and you would yield!"

sentences.zh: 驅毅者以刃斫其脛，毅不屈而死。

translations.literal: Those who drove Yi struck his shins with blades, and Yi died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Those escorting Yi hacked at his shins with blades, and he died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 贈曹州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 王晦，字子明，澤州高平人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Gaoping in Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, styled Ziming, came from Gaoping in Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 少負氣自渼，常慕張詠之為人，友妻與人有私，晦手刃殺之。

translations.literal: In youth he was proud and self-indulgent, often admired Zhang Yong's conduct; when a friend's wife had an affair with another man, Hui killed her with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was proud and headstrong and often admired the example of Zhang Yong. When a friend's wife took a lover, Hui killed her with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 中明昌二年進士，調長葛主簿，有能聲。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Mingchang, was assigned as chief clerk of Changge, and won a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Mingchang 2, was assigned as chief clerk of Changge, and earned a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 察廉除遼東路轉運司都勾判官，提刑司舉其能，轉北京轉運戶籍判官。

translations.literal: After an integrity inspection he was appointed chief auditor of the Liaodong Circuit Transport Commission; the Judicial Commission commended his ability and he was transferred to household registration judge of the Beijing Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After an integrity inspection he became chief auditor of the Liaodong Circuit Transport Commission. The Judicial Commission commended his talent, and he was transferred to household registration judge on the Beijing Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 遷安陽令，累除簽陝西西路按察司事，改平涼治中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Anyang, then successively appointed registrar of the Shaanxi West Circuit Surveillance Commission, and changed to Administrative Aide of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Magistrate of Anyang, then served successively as registrar of the Shaanxi West Circuit Surveillance Commission before becoming Administrative Aide of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 召為少府少監，遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Deputy Director of the Court of the Palace Storehouses and promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Deputy Director of the Court of the Palace Storehouses and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，中都戒嚴，或舉晦有將帥才，俾募人自將，得死士萬餘統之。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyou, when the Central Capital was under martial law, someone recommended Hui as having talent for generalship; he was ordered to recruit men and lead them himself, and obtained more than ten thousand death-dedicated troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou, when the Central Capital was placed under martial law, Hui was recommended as a man of military talent. He was ordered to raise troops and command them himself, and mustered more than ten thousand hardened fighters.

sentences.zh: 率所統衛送通州粟入中都，有功，遷霍王傅。

translations.literal: Leading his command he escorted grain from Tongzhou into the Central Capital; for this merit he was promoted to Tutor of Prince Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Leading his troops, he escorted Tongzhou grain into the Central Capital. For this service he was promoted to Tutor of Prince Huo.

sentences.zh: 以部兵守順州。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Shunzhou with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He took his troops to garrison Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 通州圍急，晦攻牛欄山以解通州之圍。

translations.literal: When the siege of Tongzhou grew desperate, Hui attacked Niulan Mountain to break the encirclement of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhou's siege grew desperate, Hui attacked Niulan Mountain to lift the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 賜賚優渥，遷翰林侍讀學士，加勸農使。

translations.literal: He was richly rewarded and promoted to Hanlin Attendant Reader and Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He received rich rewards and was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Reader and Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 九月，順州受兵，晦有別部在滄、景，遣人突圍召之，眾皆踴躍思奮，而主者不肯發。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shunzhou came under attack; Hui had a separate detachment at Cang and Jing and sent men to break out and summon them; all were eager and yearned to fight, but the man in charge would not dispatch them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shunzhou came under attack. Hui had another detachment at Cang and Jing and sent men to break out and summon them. The troops were eager to march, but the officer in command refused to release them.

sentences.zh: 王臻，晦之故部曲也，免胄出見，且拜曰：「事急矣，自苦何為，苟能相從，可不失富貴。」

translations.literal: Wang Zhen, once Hui's personal retainer, removed his helmet and came out to see him, bowing and saying: "The crisis is upon us—why torment yourself? If you will join me, you need not lose wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, once Hui's personal retainer, removed his helmet and came out to see him. Bowing, he said, "The crisis is upon us—why torment yourself? If you come with me, you need not forfeit wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 晦曰：「朝廷何負汝耶？」

translations.literal: Hui said: "What has the court done to wrong you?
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "What has the court ever done to wrong you?"

sentences.zh: 臻曰：「臻雖負國，不忍負公。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Though I have wronged the state, I cannot wrong you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Though I have betrayed the state, I cannot betray you, my lord."

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: At this he wept.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, he wept.

sentences.zh: 晦叱曰：「吾年六十，致位三品，死則吾分，詎從汝耶。」

translations.literal: Hui rebuked him: "I am sixty; I have risen to the third rank—death is my portion. How could I follow you?
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebuked him: "I am sixty years old and have risen to the third rank. Death is my due. How could I follow you?"

sentences.zh: 將射之，臻掩泣而去。

translations.literal: He was about to shoot him; Zhen covered his face, weeping, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to shoot him. Zhen covered his face, weeping, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 無何，將士縋城出降，晦被執，不肯降，遂就死。

translations.literal: Before long the officers and soldiers lowered themselves by rope over the wall to surrender; Hui was captured, would not submit, and so met his death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the officers and soldiers lowered themselves over the wall by rope to surrender. Hui was captured, refused to submit, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，晦就執，謂其愛將牛鬥曰：「若能死乎？」

translations.literal: When Hui was first taken, he asked his cherished commander Niu Dou: "Can you die?
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was first taken, he asked his trusted commander Niu Dou, "Are you willing to die?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「鬥蒙公見知，安忍獨生。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Dou received your trust—how could I bear to live alone?
translations.idiomatic: Niu Dou answered, "You honored me with your trust. How could I bear to live on alone?"

sentences.zh: 並見殺。

translations.literal: Both were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Both were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈榮祿大夫、樞密副使，仍命有司立碑，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously granted Ronglu Dafu and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and the authorities were ordered to erect a stele with seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Ronglu Dafu and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and ordered the authorities to raise a memorial stele with sacrifices at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 錄其子汝霖為筆硯承奉。

translations.literal: His son Rulin was enrolled as Brush-and-Ink Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rulin was appointed Brush-and-Ink Attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊鷹揚

translations.literal: Qi Yingyang
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yingyang

sentences.zh: 齊鷹揚，淄州軍事判官。

translations.literal: Qi Yingyang, military aide of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yingyang was military aide of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 楊敏中，屯留縣尉致仕。

translations.literal: Yang Minzhong, retired county captain of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Minzhong was the retired county captain of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 張乞驢，淄州民。

translations.literal: Zhang Qilu, a commoner of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qilu was a commoner of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，大元兵取淄州，鷹揚等募兵備禦，城破，率眾巷戰。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyou the Great Yuan army took Zizhou; Yingyang and the others recruited troops to prepare the defense; when the city fell they led the crowd in street fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou the Great Yuan army seized Zizhou. Yingyang and the others raised troops to prepare the defense, and when the city fell they led the people in street fighting.

sentences.zh: 鷹揚等三人創甚被執，欲降之，鷹揚伺守者稍怠，即起奪槊殺數人，與敏中、乞驢皆不屈以死。

translations.literal: Yingyang and the three others were badly wounded and captured; wishing to make them surrender, Yingyang watched until his guards slackened slightly, then sprang up, seized a spear, and killed several men; Yingyang, Minzhong, and Qilu all died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyang and the other three were gravely wounded and taken prisoner. As their captors tried to force their surrender, Yingyang waited until the guards relaxed, then sprang up, seized a spear, and killed several men. Yingyang, Minzhong, and Qilu all died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 詔贈鷹揚嘉議大夫、淄州刺史，仍立廟於州，以時致祭。

translations.literal: By edict Yingyang was posthumously granted Jiayi Dafu and Prefect of Zizhou, and a temple was ordered erected in the prefecture with seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Yingyang as Jiayi Dafu and Prefect of Zizhou, and ordered a temple raised in the prefecture with sacrifices at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 敏中贈昭勇大將軍、同知橫海軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Minzhong was posthumously granted Zhaoyong Da Jiangjun and Vice Commissioner of the Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong was posthumously made Zhaoyong Da Jiangjun and Vice Commissioner of the Henghai Army.

sentences.zh: 乞驢特贈宣武將軍、同知淄州軍州事。

translations.literal: Qilu was specially posthumously granted Xuanwu Jiangjun and Vice Prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qilu was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Xuanwu Jiangjun and Vice Prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 朮甲法心

translations.literal: Paijia Faxin
translations.idiomatic: Paijia Faxin

sentences.zh: 朮甲法心，薊州猛安人。

translations.literal: Paijia Faxin was a native of a military colony in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Paijia Faxin came from a military colony in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 官至北京副留守。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，為提控，與同知順州軍州事溫蒂罕咬查剌俱守密雲縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, as command officer he joined Wendihan Yaochala, Vice Prefect of Shunzhou, in defending Miyun County.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2, serving as command officer, he joined Wendihan Yaochala, Vice Prefect of Shunzhou, in the defense of Miyun County.

sentences.zh: 法心家屬在薊州，大元兵得之，以示法心曰：「若速降當以付汝，否則殺之。」

translations.literal: Faxin's family members were in Jizhou; the Great Yuan army captured them and showed them to Faxin, saying: "If you surrender promptly we shall deliver them to you; otherwise we shall kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Faxin's family were in Jizhou. The Great Yuan army captured them and paraded them before him, saying, "Surrender at once and we will release them to you. Otherwise we will kill them."

sentences.zh: 法心曰：「吾事本朝受厚恩，戰則速戰，終不能降也，豈以家人死生為計耶。」

translations.literal: Faxin said: "I serve the dynasty and have received deep favor—when there is battle, let battle come quickly; I can never surrender. How could I calculate on the life or death of my family?
translations.idiomatic: Faxin said, "I serve this dynasty and have received its deep bounty. When battle comes, let it come swiftly—I can never surrender. How could I weigh my family's lives in the balance?"

sentences.zh: 城破，死於陣。

translations.literal: When the city fell he died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he died fighting.

sentences.zh: 咬查剌被執，亦不屈而死。

translations.literal: Yaochala was captured and likewise died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochala was taken prisoner and likewise died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 盤安軍節度判官蒲察颭舍與雞澤縣令溫蒂罕十方奴同守薊州，眾潰而出，颭舍、十方奴死之。

translations.literal: Pucha Zhanshe, military judge of the Pan'an Army, and Wendihan Shifangnu, Magistrate of Jize County, jointly defended Jizhou; the troops collapsed and fled outward, and Zhanshe and Shifangnu died.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Zhanshe, military judge of the Pan'an Army, and Wendihan Shifangnu, Magistrate of Jize County, defended Jizhou together. When the army broke and fled the city, Zhanshe and Shifangnu were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈法心開府儀同三司、樞密副使，封宿國公，咬查剌鎮國上將軍、順州刺史，颭舍金紫光祿大夫、薊州刺史，十方奴鎮國上將軍、薊州刺史。

translations.literal: By edict Faxin was posthumously granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Su; Yaochala was granted Zhenguo Upper General and Prefect of Shunzhou; Zhanshe was granted Jinzi Guanglu Dafu and Prefect of Jizhou; Shifangnu was granted Zhenguo Upper General and Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Faxin as Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, creating him Duke of Su; Yaochala as Zhenguo Upper General and Prefect of Shunzhou; Zhanshe as Jinzi Guanglu Dafu and Prefect of Jizhou; and Shifangnu as Zhenguo Upper General and Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 仍命樹碑，以時致祭

translations.literal: They were also ordered memorial steles erected and seasonal sacrifices performed.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial steles were also ordered for them, with sacrifices at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 高錫，字永之，德基子。

translations.literal: Gao Xi, courtesy name Yongzhi, was Deji's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xi, styled Yongzhi, was the son of Deji.

sentences.zh: 以廕補官。

translations.literal: He entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 積勞調淄州酒使，課最。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he was transferred to wine commissioner of Zizhou, where his performance ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Through long service he was transferred to wine commissioner of Zizhou, where his performance ranked first.

sentences.zh: 遷平鄉令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Magistrate of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 察廉遷遼東路轉運支度判官、太倉使、法物庫使、兼尚林置直長、提舉都城所，曆北京、遼東轉運副使、同知南京路轉運使事。

translations.literal: After an integrity inspection he was promoted to expense judge of the Liaodong Circuit Transport Commission, Commissioner of the Grand Granary, Commissioner of the Ritual Objects Store, concurrent Director of the Imperial Forest Plantation, and Commissioner of the Metropolitan Capital Office; he served as Deputy Transport Commissioner of Beijing and Liaodong and Vice Transport Commissioner of the Nanjing Route.
translations.idiomatic: After an integrity review he became expense judge on the Liaodong Transport Commission, commissioner of the Grand Granary and the Ritual Objects Store, concurrent director of the Imperial Forest Plantation, and commissioner of the Metropolitan Capital Office, then served as deputy transport commissioner for Beijing and Liaodong and vice transport commissioner on the Nanjing circuit.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，累遷河北東路按察轉運使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was repeatedly promoted to Surveillance and Transport Commissioner of the Hebei East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he rose to Surveillance and Transport Commissioner of the Hebei East circuit.

sentences.zh: 城破，遂自投城下而死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he thereupon cast himself from the wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he threw himself from the battlements and died.
